sources.note: A disciplined post-MD-059 handover audit of the F3/F4 KnowledgeOS candidate-model comparison research line: an A-K F4 completeness matrix, an L-Q F3<->F4 readiness matrix (finding the comparison currently ill-typed, not merely untested), an R-T GA-001/GA-038 blocker analysis, a strict same-day/consuming-vs-independent provenance-audit rule, a minimal dependency chain isolating decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) as the smallest next research act, and a final verdict NOT READY -- REMAINING EVIDENCE/GOVERNANCE GAP. New research territory for this extraction pass (MD-058/MD-059/F3/F4/GA-001/GA-038 not found in the object index from earlier batches).

rows.anchor: I treated MD-058 and MD-059 as the frozen handover boundary and used only their recorded evidence/provenance and the primary corpus sources they explicitly relied upon. I did not perform new theory, reconciliation, model selection, F3<->F4 bridging, external literature research, or implementation. F4 is semantically instantiated in form, but not closed enough to make its satisfaction semantics computable; and it is not yet typed into a common observation space with F3. The two remaining blockers are therefore distinct: internal F4 closure and cross-model bridging.
rows.statement: States the audit's decisive finding and self-imposed scope boundary: F4 is instantiated in form but not computationally closed, and separately not yet typed into a common observation space with F3 -- two genuinely distinct blockers (internal F4 closure vs cross-model bridging), both named by MD-059 as separate unauthorized next acts.

rows.anchor: F4 completeness matrix A-K: A K_t variant census PARTIALLY FOUND (9+ mutually unreconciled variants, only 1 of 11 named components concretely typed); B component semantics NOT FOUND (only Sigma_t=(A,S,R,V,C) concretely defined, in one variant only); C relationships among variants CONFLICTING (mutually unreconciled, no component-level consistency established); D corpus-grounded common semantic core NOT FOUND; E R_t semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (Req(EC_t) exists as formal input but satisfaction predicates remain multiply defined/contested); F Sat(K_t,r) semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (shape frozen, but computing Sat requires K_t component semantics which are incomplete -- defined in form but not computationally closed); G decomposition-independent Sat NOT FOUND (the principal internal F4 blocker); H K_t->K_{t+1} transition semantics CONFLICTING (delta(K_t,e_t) and the P-12/P-13 family unresolved); I F4 Obs PARTIALLY FOUND (constructible in form, not computable); J F4 Beh PARTIALLY FOUND (general slot exists, no executable F4 Beh, classified UNAVAILABLE); K F4 Trace PARTIALLY FOUND (general machinery exists, no F4-specific instances).
rows.statement: Gives the full eleven-item (A-K) F4 completeness matrix distinguishing what exists in form/shape from what is computationally closed across the K_t variant census, component semantics, R_t/Sat semantics, and F4's Obs/Beh/Trace, concluding this is why MD-059 did not describe F4 as simply absent -- the semantic shell is real but instantiation is incomplete.

rows.anchor: F3<->F4 readiness matrix L-Q: L F3 observation semantics FOUND (Beh_c(K):=Reach(Ops(K)), the only candidate with real instantiated semantics); M F4 observation semantics PARTIALLY FOUND (formally constructible, not computable since Sat is not closed); N atoms<->requirements bridge NOT FOUND (F3 outputs reached atoms, F4 outputs satisfied requirements, no corpus document bridges these types); O common observation domain NOT FOUND (different codomains, no common Q,O can be posed without inventing the bridge); P common behaviour/trace domain NOT FOUND (F3 has instantiated behaviour, F4 does not); Q formal F3<->F4 equivalence relation NOT FOUND (MD-058 derived the general shape Obs-equality but not the corpus-intended ≡, and its cross-candidate matrix left all 15 pairs unresolved).
rows.statement: Gives the full six-item (L-Q) F3<->F4 readiness matrix, establishing F3 as the only model with real instantiated observation semantics and F4 as merely formally constructible, with the critical N/O finding that F3 and F4 currently have no corpus-grounded bridge between their output types (atoms vs satisfied requirements) at all.

rows.anchor: K1 approx_{Q,O} K2 iff Obs_{Q,O}(K1)=Obs_{Q,O}(K2). But this is not a completed F3<->F4 equivalence result. MD-058 explicitly says that Q,O remain open and that this does not recover the corpus-intended stronger equiv. So: The equivalence machinery exists; the F3/F4 semantic inputs required to instantiate it do not.
rows.statement: Clarifies that MD-058's general equivalence formula (K1 approx K2 iff their Q,O-relative observations match) is real mathematics but not itself a completed F3<->F4 equivalence result, since the Q,O parameters remain open and cannot recover the corpus-intended stronger equivalence relation -- the machinery exists but the semantic inputs to instantiate it do not.

rows.anchor: GA-001/GA-038 readiness R-T: R evidence sufficient for GA-001 NOT FOUND (MD-059 sharpened this to a type mismatch: atoms vs requirements); S evidence sufficient for GA-038 NOT FOUND (MD-023 found no corpus-justified canonicalization criterion, the sole positive precedent being explicit governance ratification of Delta_t, not mathematical selection); T evidence to compare F4 with another candidate beyond F3 NOT FOUND (all 15 pairwise comparisons in MD-058's matrix remained unresolved). GA-001 is blocked by missing comparable semantic types, not by lack of an equivalence formula. GA-038 is also not a hidden computational problem at present ... GA-038 cannot legitimately be marked solved merely because F4 becomes computable.
rows.statement: Assesses both higher-level governance objectives GA-001 and GA-038 as unchanged/blocked, sharply distinguishing GA-001's blocker (a named type mismatch between atoms and requirements, not a missing equivalence formula) from GA-038's blocker (absence of any corpus-grounded canonicalization criterion, with the only successful precedent being governance ratification rather than mathematical selection), and explicitly warning that F4 becoming computable would not by itself solve GA-038.

rows.anchor: The externally supplied analysis encountered during MD-059 must not be counted as independent corroboration. MD-059 established that it: was created the same day, explicitly cited MD-058, was therefore a response to MD-058 rather than prior evidence, was classified as same-day, MD-058-consuming re-analysis. It is useful as a cross-check, but not admissible as independent corroboration of the F4 state.
rows.statement: Applies a strict provenance rule: an externally supplied analysis encountered during MD-059, though created the same day and citing MD-058, is classified as same-day/MD-058-consuming re-analysis rather than independent prior evidence, and is therefore admissible only as a cross-check, never as independent corroboration of F4's state.

rows.anchor: [DEF-15] is in M0043, a primary corpus source dated 2026-09-02. MD-059 discovered it on 2026-09-09. Therefore: the discovery was same-day relative to MD-059; the underlying evidence predates MD-059; it is not derivative of MD-059. It corrected MD-058's provenance interpretation, but did not invalidate MD-058's mathematical derivation.
rows.statement: Draws a fine provenance distinction for [DEF-15]: although discovered the same day as MD-059, its underlying evidence (M0043, dated 2026-09-02) genuinely predates MD-059, so it counts as legitimate prior evidence (unlike the externally-supplied same-day analysis) that corrects MD-058's provenance interpretation without invalidating its mathematical derivation.

rows.anchor: theory-extraction/ / Lane-T K3 / Omega / T-K1 / T-K2 -- MD-059 explicitly kept these firewalled throughout. Therefore those materials must not silently become F4 evidence in this handover.
rows.statement: Notes that materials from another research lane (Lane-T / theory-extraction, including K3/Omega/T-K1/T-K2) were explicitly firewalled by MD-059 and must not be silently absorbed as F4 evidence in this or any handover.

rows.anchor: Delta_t = {r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)} -- Defined and frozen. This is not the blocker. Sat(K_t,r) -- Defined in shape, not computationally closed. defined != computable. Obs_F4 -- Constructible in form, not computable. That is stronger than 'not found' but weaker than 'implemented.' Beh_F4/Trace_F4 -- General semantic slots exist; F4-specific instantiation unavailable. F3<->F4 -- Not merely untested. It is presently ill-typed as a comparison because Obs_F3 subseteq reached atoms while Obs_F4 subseteq satisfied requirements. There is no corpus-grounded mapping between these spaces.
rows.statement: States five precise state distinctions to preserve exactly: Delta_t is frozen and not the blocker; Sat is defined-in-shape but not computable (defined != computable); Obs_F4 is constructible-but-not-computable (a third state between 'not found' and 'implemented'); Beh_F4/Trace_F4 have general slots but no F4-specific instantiation; and the F3<->F4 comparison is not merely untested but presently ill-typed, since Obs_F3 and Obs_F4 live in different, unbridged codomains (reached atoms vs satisfied requirements).

rows.anchor: Minimal remaining dependency chain: K_t component semantics -> decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) -> computable F4 Obs_F4 -> [F4 Beh_F4/Trace_F4 <- transition/composition semantics] -> F4 semantic instantiation -> [F3 observation semantics, F4 observation semantics] -> atoms<->requirements -> common observation domain -> well-posed F3<->F4 comparison -> cross-model equivalence -> [GA-001, evidence relevant to GA-038 but NOT sufficient by itself]. F4 completion does not automatically solve GA-038. GA-001 cannot be reached merely by having Obs_F4; the atom/requirement type mismatch still has to be resolved by admissible evidence.
rows.statement: Lays out the full minimal dependency chain from K_t component semantics through to GA-001/GA-038, explicitly stating this reconstructs an existing corpus-supported chain rather than introducing a new one, and reiterating that neither GA-001 nor GA-038 follows automatically even once F4 is completed.

rows.anchor: MD-059 records: 1. reconcile the 9+ K_t variants enough to provide a decomposition-independent Sat body; 2. build the missing atoms<->requirements bridge. For the smallest fundamental blocker, the first act is prior: Research Act: establish whether the existing corpus contains sufficient evidence for a decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) semantics across the existing K_t variants. Without Sat, Obs_F4 is not computable. Without Obs_F4, F4 has no comparable instantiated observation semantics. Without F4 semantics, the F3<->F4 comparison cannot advance. GA-001 therefore cannot advance through F4. The atoms<->requirements bridge is a second, independent blocker, but even a perfect bridge cannot make Sat(K_t,r) computable. That research act has not been executed here.
rows.statement: Identifies the single smallest fundamental next research act as determining whether the existing corpus already contains sufficient evidence for a decomposition-independent Sat(K_t,r) (prior to actually reconciling the 9+ K_t variants), arguing it is logically prior to the separately-needed atoms<->requirements bridge since even a perfect bridge cannot make Sat computable; explicitly states this act has not been executed in this document.

rows.anchor: Final handover state table: Delta_t FOUND/FROZEN; Sat shape FOUND/FROZEN; K_t family PARTIALLY FOUND (9+ unreconciled variants); K_t component semantics INSUFFICIENT; computable Sat NOT AVAILABLE; computable Obs_F4 NOT AVAILABLE; F4 Beh NOT AVAILABLE; F4 Trace NOT AVAILABLE; F3 Obs FOUND; atoms<->requirements bridge NOT FOUND; common observation domain NOT FOUND; F3<->F4 equivalence NOT FOUND/NOT WELL-POSED; GA-001 UNCHANGED-BLOCKED; GA-038 UNCHANGED-BLOCKED; F4 vs another candidate beyond F3 NOT AVAILABLE; canonical K_t NOT SELECTED; external evidence NOT used as independent corroboration; new theory NONE; implementation NONE. MD-059 itself confirms the hard-stop boundary: no candidate was selected, no equiv_sem was adopted, no F1-F8 merge occurred, and no MD-060 was opened. Handover verdict: NOT READY -- REMAINING EVIDENCE/GOVERNANCE GAP.
rows.statement: Consolidates the entire audit into a final nineteen-row state table and delivers the explicit handover verdict NOT READY -- REMAINING EVIDENCE/GOVERNANCE GAP, confirming MD-059's own hard-stop boundary (no candidate selected, no equivalence relation adopted, no F1-F8 merge, no MD-060 opened).

rows.anchor: The historical corpus does contain more of the backbone than the earlier handover stated. The important correction is that the remaining problem is not absence of notation or conceptual primitives; it is the absence of a closed, mutually typed, F4-specific operational composition.
rows.statement: Corrects the earlier handover's framing: the historical corpus contains substantially more semantic backbone (notation and conceptual primitives) than previously credited; the actual remaining problem is the absence of a closed, mutually typed, F4-specific operational composition linking those primitives, not their absence.

lineage_claims.quote: The historical corpus does contain more of the backbone than the earlier handover stated.

rows.anchor: K_t in K-blackboard, K-blackboard = space of admissible semantic epistemic states. It explicitly refuses to make K_t universally equal to a tuple and instead distinguishes semantic state from representation. K_t=(Content,Support,Uncertainty,Model,Alternatives,History,Identity,Context,Inquiry,Status) but explicitly a semantic decomposition, not a mandatory storage tuple. The most explicit later Model-B form is the 11-component tuple K_t=(A_t,R_t,E_t,Sigma_t,H_t,Z_t,L_t,T_t,G_t,C_t,M_t), but that family is not selected by the abstract DEF-11 formulation. Verdict: K_t in K-blackboard FOUND-UNTYPED; Concrete Model-B K_t CONFLICTING. There is no evidence selecting one concrete Model-B formulation.
rows.statement: Establishes that the historical corpus defines K_t as an abstract semantic epistemic state (K_t in K-blackboard, deliberately not reduced to a mandatory tuple, with a ten-field semantic decomposition explicitly marked non-mandatory) alongside a separate, unselected 11-component concrete Model-B tuple family, verdict FOUND-UNTYPED for the abstract form and CONFLICTING for the concrete family, with no evidence selecting between the concrete formulations.

rows.anchor: r(K_t)=x_t. Representation carrier (X_r, A_r) and family R-script={R_r: r in R}, R_r: K-blackboard <-> X_r. No single representation is automatically the KnowledgeOS ontology. Missing: the mathematical type of r; whether every r is a function; whether R_r is total/partial/injective/surjective/invertible/merely relational; the precise type of x_t; admissibility conditions. Notation collision: in representation theory r denotes a representation; in gap theory r denotes an epistemic requirement r=(id,type,scope,content,standard,priority,validity). The corpus does not establish that these two uses of r are the same object.
rows.statement: Establishes the representation function r(K_t)=x_t with a representation carrier and family, explicitly noting no representation is automatically canonical, but leaves the mathematical type of r, its totality/injectivity/invertibility properties, and x_t's precise type unclosed; identifies a genuine notation collision where 'r' denotes a representation in one theory and a seven-field epistemic requirement in another, with the corpus never establishing these are the same object. Verdict: FOUND-UNTYPED.

rows.anchor: Obs: O_t^s = Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t), and epistemic observables as functions in a measurable setting. But this does not establish Obs_F4: K-blackboard -> O_F4. There is no historical rule showing that Obs_F4(K_t) is obtained from r(K_t)=x_t, from EC, or from Sat. Verdict: Generic Obs FOUND-TYPED; F4-specific Obs_F4 NOT FOUND.
rows.statement: Finds a generic, formally typed historical Obs function (O_t^s=Obs(s,W_t,m_t,c_t)) but no rule deriving an F4-specific Obs_F4 from any of r(K_t), EC, or Sat, verdict: generic Obs FOUND-TYPED, F4-specific Obs_F4 NOT FOUND.

rows.anchor: EC_t = EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t), the epistemic contract, used to define I(EC_t)={K in K-blackboard: Sat(K,EC_t)} and Adequate(K_t,EC_t) iff Sat(K_t,EC_t). Missing: contract structure present; contract construction algorithm absent; fully grounded Sat only partial. No source establishes that EC_t is identical to C_KOS. They should therefore remain separate. Verdict: EC FOUND-UNTYPED.
rows.statement: Establishes the epistemic contract EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t) with its role in defining an admissible ideal region and adequacy, but finds no construction algorithm for EC_t and no evidence that EC_t is identical to C_KOS (the two should remain separate concepts), verdict FOUND-UNTYPED.

rows.anchor: The ten Sat questions -- decisive audit: 1. Domain of K_t? K-blackboard proposed, exact structure OPEN. 2. Type of r? seven-field tuple proposed. 3. Codomain? {0,1} explicitly proposed; competing top/bot/U sub-semantics also exist. 4. Total/partial? NOT ESTABLISHED. 5. Evidence required? categories discussed, no complete evaluator. 6. Meaning of 1? requirement satisfied. 7. Meaning of 0? requirement unsatisfied. 8. Insufficient evidence? NOT CLOSED, candidate Unknown semantics exist. 9. Is UNKNOWN distinct? general theory yes, F4 Sat treatment NOT ESTABLISHED. 10. Deterministic/reproducible? NO -- no complete evaluation algorithm. Two engineers cannot currently compute the same Sat(K_t,r) from corpus-defined rules alone.
rows.statement: Runs a ten-question decisive audit of Sat(K_t,r) against the historical corpus, finding the codomain itself contested (binary {0,1} vs a ternary top/bot/Unknown sub-semantics with no authorized selection), totality/evidence-sufficiency/insufficient-evidence-treatment all unclosed, and concludes with a definitive negative reproducibility test: two engineers cannot currently compute the same Sat(K_t,r) result from corpus-defined rules alone.

rows.anchor: Delta_t = {r in R_t: Sat(K_t,r)=0}. It is the strongest historical F4 formula and was subsequently frozen as a constraint. R_t typed? PARTIALLY/candidate-typed. Sat typed? PARTIALLY; codomain conflicting. Sat executable? NO. Delta_t formula defined? YES. Delta_t executable? NO. Therefore: defined Delta_t != computable Delta_t. Verdict: Delta_t FOUND-UNTYPED as an operational object. The set-formula exists, but its evaluation cannot yet be executed.
rows.statement: Confirms Delta_t's set-builder formula is the strongest, frozen historical F4 formula, but derives via a five-row dependency table that it is not executable since Sat is not executable, establishing the sharp distinction defined Delta_t != computable Delta_t.

rows.anchor: Transition semantics: K_{t+1}=T(K_t,E_{t+1},Q_t,C_t,EC_t,A_t) and H_{t+1}=H_t union {transition_t}; also K_{t+1}=Transition(K_t,Operation,Parameters) with remaining work to define exact operation semantics/pre/postconditions; also H_t=(e_0,...,e_{t-1}), H_{t+1}=H_t || e_t, Replay(K_0,H_t)=K_t. These must not be collapsed: T, delta, Transition, event-based, operation-based, history, replay are not established as one formally identical transition system. The later persistence audit explicitly records that the tau_1..tau_11 items are transition CLASSES, not functions. Do not equate the tau classes with delta.
rows.statement: Catalogs at least four distinct historical transition-semantics formulations (T-based, event-based Transition/Operation, history-append with Replay, and tau_1..tau_11 transition classes) and explicitly warns against collapsing them into one formally identical transition system, particularly against equating the tau classes (transition classes, not functions) with delta.

rows.anchor: Verdicts: T FOUND-UNTYPED; delta PARTIALLY GROUNDED; tau_1..tau_11 FOUND-UNTYPED/OPEN as functions; H_t FOUND-UNTYPED; K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) as universal F4 rule NOT ESTABLISHED; Replay PROPOSED, not established as F4 semantics.
rows.statement: Gives per-object verdicts for the six transition-related historical constructs, none reaching a closed, established F4-wide status.

rows.anchor: Semantic equivalence: r1 equiv_sem r2, with [[r1(x)]]=[[r2(y)]] and a behavioural formulation r1 equiv_sem r2 iff B_r1=B_r2 over an admissible test domain. Established: operands are representations; semantic-equivalence notation; a semantic-meaning criterion in prose; a behavioural formulation. Not established: the semantic interpretation function [[.]]; the admissible test domain; B_r; the exact codomain of B; the F4 observable interface; whether the relation is computed from Sat, Obs, Beh, or another semantic object. The historical source itself recognises the circularity problem: saying representations are equivalent because they have the same meaning does not supply an independent test. Verdict: equiv_sem FOUND-UNTYPED -- defined as a historical relation shape, not operationally computable. And critically: equiv_sem compares representations, whereas Sat(K_t,r) uses r as a requirement. Those two rs must not be conflated.
rows.statement: Establishes that semantic equivalence (equiv_sem) has real historical notation and a behavioural formulation over representations, but the historical source itself flags an unresolved circularity (meaning-based equivalence lacks an independent test), and reiterates that this equiv_sem's 'r' (a representation) must never be conflated with Sat's 'r' (a requirement) -- the same notation collision named earlier in the document.

rows.anchor: F4 specificity audit (table): K_t in K-blackboard F4-SPECIFIC UNCLEAR; concrete Model-B K_t variants F4-SPECIFIC; K-blackboard GENERAL; r(K_t)=x_t GENERAL; Obs(s,W,m,c) GENERAL; EC(S,G,Q,C) GENERAL/F4-adjacent; Sat(K_t,r) F4-SPECIFIC FORM, GENERAL SEMANTIC CONTENT; R_t/Req(EC_t) F4-ADJACENT; Delta_t F4-SPECIFIC; T/delta GENERAL/MULTIPLE LINEAGES; H_t GENERAL/UNCLEAR; equiv_sem GENERAL. A historical semantic construct mentioning K_t is not automatically a Model-B aggregate/state definition.
rows.statement: Classifies twelve historical objects by whether each is F4-specific, general, or adjacent, establishing the DDD boundary principle that a historical construct merely mentioning K_t is not automatically a Model-B aggregate/state definition.

rows.anchor: Composition test (13 arrows): K_t -> r(K_t)=x_t DIRECT; K_t -> Obs NO EVIDENCED LINK; r(K_t)=x_t -> Obs NO EVIDENCED LINK; Obs -> EC NO EVIDENCED LINK; EC -> R_t/Req(EC_t) DIRECT but construction algorithm open; K_t+r -> Sat(K_t,r) DIRECT but only at definitional/formula level; Sat -> Delta_t DIRECT; Delta_t -> T/delta NO EVIDENCED LINK; T/delta -> H_t CORROBORATED, not closed F4-specific; H_t -> equiv_sem NO EVIDENCED LINK; r1,r2 -> equiv_sem DIRECT; Sat -> equiv_sem NO EVIDENCED LINK; Obs -> equiv_sem STRUCTURAL RESEMBLANCE. The corpus does not contain one closed semantic pipeline. It contains several genuine fragments ... but the crucial cross-links are absent. This is not merely 'one missing function.' It is a partially composed semantic system.
rows.statement: Runs a thirteen-arrow composition test across the full semantic chain from K_t to equiv_sem, finding five DIRECT links, one CORROBORATED link, one STRUCTURAL RESEMBLANCE, and six with NO EVIDENCED LINK at all, concluding the corpus is not merely missing one function but constitutes a genuinely partially composed semantic system with several disconnected fragments.

rows.anchor: Maximum three blockers. Blocker 1 -- K_t semantic binding: no closed mathematical type for K-blackboard and no evidence binding one concrete representation to the abstract semantic state without a modelling choice; this blocks the domain on which Sat operates. Blocker 2 -- closed satisfaction semantics: the corpus does not close evidence sufficiency, acceptance standard, temporal validity, uncertainty, model validity, insufficient-evidence treatment, or binary-vs-unknown-aware outcome semantics; this is the direct blocker to computing Sat and therefore Delta_t. Blocker 3 -- semantic composition/observable binding: the chain K_t -> r(K_t) -> Obs_F4 -> EC -> Sat -> Delta_t -> T/delta -> H_t has several explicit individual arrows but the cross-links required for a single F4 semantic system are missing; this blocks later F4 semantic equivalence and a well-typed F3<->F4 comparison.
rows.statement: Reduces the entire historical audit to exactly three blockers: (1) no closed mathematical type for K-blackboard binding the abstract semantic state to a concrete representation, (2) no computable Sat evaluator across seven named unresolved dimensions, and (3) the missing cross-links needed to compose the individual historical fragments into one F4-specific semantic system.

rows.anchor: Decisive conclusion C -- Backbone is only partially composed. The historical corpus contains a genuine semantic backbone: K_t, K-blackboard, r, x_t, Obs, EC, Sat, R_t, Delta_t, T, H_t, equiv_sem. So the earlier statement 'the historical semantic primitives are absent' would be incorrect. But the backbone is not operationally closed. Sat not computable => Delta_t not computable => F4 equivalence not evaluable, and the F3<->F4 comparison remains ill-posed because no F4-specific observation domain has been established. No canonicalization, equivalence resolution, GA-001/GA-038 work, or implementation follows from this audit. |K|=11, [REC], UNFROZEN, firewall intact.
rows.statement: Delivers the decisive conclusion (labeled option C): the twelve-object semantic backbone genuinely exists in the corpus (correcting any prior 'primitives absent' framing) but remains operationally uncomposed, restating the implication chain Sat-not-computable => Delta_t-not-computable => F4-equivalence-not-evaluable, and explicitly disclaiming any canonicalization, equivalence resolution, GA-001/GA-038 progress, or implementation as following from this audit.

rows.anchor: I treated later summaries as evidence about what earlier work claimed, not as proof that the claimed semantics were actually established. This distinction is decisive here.
rows.statement: States an explicit methodological discipline for this and the sibling audits: treat later summaries only as evidence of what earlier work claimed, never as proof the claimed semantics were actually established -- named as the decisive discipline separating this audit series from naive citation-counting.

rows.anchor: The underlying predicates are themselves unresolved or multiply defined, including C_KOS, |=, Contr, >=, delta, and Qualify.
rows.statement: Lists six further underlying predicates feeding into Sat's evaluation that are themselves unresolved or multiply defined across the corpus: C_KOS, the satisfaction/entailment relation, Contr, the epistemic ordering relation, delta, and Qualify.

rows.anchor: It was explicitly frozen in Model B through M0132, with the important qualification that the freeze was 'freeze-as-constraint, not conclusion.'
rows.statement: Clarifies that Delta_t's freeze in Model B (via M0132) was explicitly a 'freeze-as-constraint, not conclusion', a nuance not stated in this exact phrasing in the sibling audits (S2888, S2889, S2891) of this same batch.

rows.anchor: semantic fragments exist =/=> semantic composition exists. The historical F4 audit reaches exactly this conclusion: F4 has the K_t, Delta_t, R_t, Sat vocabulary, but lacks a complete F4-specific observation, behaviour, trace, transition and satisfaction construction.
rows.statement: States the composition test's core lesson as a compact non-implication (semantic fragments existing does not imply semantic composition existing), restating the shared conclusion of this document's audit series that F4 has the vocabulary but not the construction.

rows.anchor: No kernel cell was changed, no alternative was selected, and no missing semantic rule was invented.
rows.statement: Restates the governing constraint observed throughout this audit series: the audit changes no kernel cell, selects no alternative among competing formulations, and invents no missing semantic rule.

rows.anchor: This is genuine pre-MD-058 evidence: the artifact is dated 2026-09-01, and the chronology establishes that this semantic-state formulation predates MD-058/059.
rows.statement: Explicitly establishes chronological provenance: the K_t in K-blackboard semantic-state formulation is dated 2026-09-01, genuinely predating MD-058/MD-059, supporting its admissibility as prior (not consuming) evidence.

rows.anchor: EC=(Purpose,Requirements,EvidenceRules,UncertaintyLimits,ConflictRules,TemporalRules,AuthorityRules) and explicitly says that EC is a first-class governance object. contract structure: clear; contract construction algorithm: not found; EC must be authored; the corpus does not establish by whom/how it is authored. The later DeriveContract(G,S)/eta line also does not solve this: the historical record specifically identifies the total-function interpretation as invalid because the available inputs do not determine the contract.
rows.statement: Adds a richer seven-field historical EC structure (Purpose/Requirements/EvidenceRules/UncertaintyLimits/ConflictRules/TemporalRules/AuthorityRules) explicitly designated a first-class governance object requiring human authorship, and records that a candidate DeriveContract(G,S)/eta total-function interpretation was explicitly rejected because available inputs do not determine the contract.

rows.anchor: Separately, the C1 lane has K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t). But that belongs to another lineage and cannot be silently imported into Model B. ... tau classes must not be equated with delta merely because both describe transitions.
rows.statement: Identifies K_{t+1}=delta(K_t,e_t) as belonging to a separate research lineage ('the C1 lane'), explicitly warning it cannot be silently imported into Model B's own transition semantics, reinforcing that transition classes (tau) must not be equated with delta merely because both describe transitions.

rows.anchor: Requested properties for equiv_sem: operands PARTIAL; domain NOT CLOSED; codomain NOT CLOSED; criterion PARTIALLY FOUND; reflexivity NOT ESTABLISHED; symmetry NOT ESTABLISHED; transitivity NOT ESTABLISHED; equivalence classes NOT ESTABLISHED; dependence on K_t NOT CLOSED; dependence on EC NOT CLOSED; dependence on observations NOT CLOSED. Therefore this is not yet ready for actual F4 equivalence evaluation.
rows.statement: Runs a formal eleven-property checklist against the historical semantic-equivalence relation equiv_sem, finding not even its basic equivalence-relation properties (reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity) or equivalence-class construction established, concluding it is not ready for actual F4 equivalence evaluation -- more granular than the circularity observation made in historical_source.md (S2889).

rows.anchor: MD-059 additionally found DEF-15 in M0043 as a primary dated corpus precedent for the same shape [of semantic equivalence].
rows.statement: Notes MD-059's discovery of DEF-15 in M0043 as an independent primary-source precedent corroborating the historical semantic-equivalence shape, consistent with the provenance analysis in handover_verdict (S2888).

rows.anchor: Decisive conclusion C -- Backbone is only partially composed. Not A, because Sat and semantic equivalence are not executable. Not merely B, because the principal issue is not one isolated missing type: the composition between historically grounded constructs is not established as an F4/Model-B semantic system. Not D as the primary conclusion, because although there are genuine competing formulations, the deeper finding is that the corpus has not established the relationships necessary to determine which alternatives constitute the same semantic object.
rows.statement: Explicitly rules out three alternative conclusions (A: backbone entirely absent; B: one isolated missing type; D: the issue is merely competing formulations) in favor of conclusion C (partially composed backbone), giving explicit reasoning for excluding each alternative -- a more structured elimination argument than the parallel conclusion in historical_source.md (S2889).

rows.anchor: Final gate state: Sat computable? NO. Delta computable? NO. F4 semantic equivalence? NO. F3<->F4 well-posed? NO. GA-001 ready? NO. GA-038 ready? NO. And importantly, nothing in this audit authorizes a choice among the competing formulations. |K|=11, [REC], UNFROZEN, firewall intact. NOT READY -- REMAINING EVIDENCE/GOVERNANCE GAP.
rows.statement: Restates the identical six-item final gate state and NOT READY verdict found in handover_verdict (S2888), independently arrived at through this parallel completion audit.

rows.anchor: The decisive blocker is Sat, but it is preceded by two structural blockers: no selected/typed F4 state carrier and no F4-specific observation/transition semantics connecting that carrier to the satisfaction test.
rows.statement: Restates the same three-blocker structure found across this document series, ordering them explicitly: an untyped F4 state carrier and missing F4-specific observation/transition semantics both precede and feed into the decisive Sat blocker.

rows.anchor: there is no corpus-defined rule saying exactly how the following cases evaluate: requirement absent != requirement contradicted != evidence insufficient != evidence inadmissible != evidence stale != evidence conflicting. The historical material itself recognizes these as epistemically distinct states.
rows.statement: Enumerates six epistemically distinct requirement/evidence states (absent, contradicted, insufficient, inadmissible, stale, conflicting) that the historical corpus recognizes as conceptually distinct but for which no corpus-defined evaluation rule exists, sharpening the general 'Sat not closed' finding into a concrete list of unaddressed cases.

rows.anchor: The notation r does not prove that the operands are representations. The historical corpus uses r both for representation-related notation and for epistemic requirements. That makes the operand type an actual unresolved issue, not a cosmetic notation problem. ... tau_i != delta for audit purposes.
rows.statement: Reinforces the r-notation collision (representation vs requirement) as a substantive unresolved-operand-type issue rather than cosmetic, and restates tau_i != delta as an audit-purposes ruling to prevent silently identifying the transition-class universe with the C1 lineage's delta function.

rows.anchor: NOT READY -- missing evidence: (1) a source-grounded, typed F4/Model-B K_t carrier; (2) F4-specific observation and closed transition semantics; (3) a closed, reproducible Sat(K_t,r) evaluation semantics. No theory has been invented or canonicalized in reaching this result. State remains: |K|=11, [REC], UNFROZEN, firewall intact.
rows.statement: Delivers the same NOT READY verdict as the sibling audits, itemized into exactly three missing-evidence categories (typed K_t carrier, F4-specific observation/transition semantics, closed Sat evaluation semantics).

rows.anchor: The corpus contains Sat as a semantic/adequacy predicate. MD-061 introduced Sat* as a concrete component-membership evaluator. Those are not the same evidential status. The MD-061 record itself explicitly says that Sat* is not corpus-native and that the result is Gate C -- CONDITIONAL CANDIDATE.
rows.statement: States the decisive distinction between corpus-native Sat (a semantic/adequacy predicate) and MD-061's Sat* (a concrete component-membership evaluator), citing MD-061's own self-classification as Gate C -- CONDITIONAL CANDIDATE, not corpus-native.

rows.anchor: vacuity test exposes this: Accept_r = Domain(component_r) or Accept_r=empty is discussed as a property of the newly constructed requirement framework, not as a previously established corpus rule.
rows.statement: Notes MD-061's own vacuity test (checking whether Accept_r trivially equals the full domain or the empty set) as further evidence that Accept_r is a property of the newly constructed framework, not a previously established corpus rule.

rows.anchor: K_t^s = Projection_s(W_<=t) conceptually, and explicitly distinguishes K_t != W_t and K_t != CompleteReality. Extract: E -> X versus Determine(X,EC) -> Status. K_t is best characterised historically as: a reconstructed/represented epistemic state grounded in evidence and observation, relative to participant/context/inquiry/contract. It is not reality itself, and it is not simply a normative ideal state. Source of epistemic grounding: FOUND. Unique F4 reconstruction function: NOT ESTABLISHED.
rows.statement: Gives a source-of-truth formulation for K_t as a participant-relative projection of world history (K_t^s=Projection_s(W_<=t)), explicitly distinguished from W_t and CompleteReality, and separates the historical Extract:E->X function from Determine(X,EC)->Status, concluding K_t's epistemic grounding is found but no unique F4 reconstruction function is established.

rows.anchor: Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) the Epistemic State Vector, with enumerated domains Acquisition/Support/Resolution/Validity/Conflict, S=A x S x R x V x C. The adversarial Sigma audit subsequently found that these five dimensions are not necessarily five homogeneous semantic axes: S=epistemic support; A=acquisition/provenance-related; R=lifecycle/resolution; V=temporal validity; C=conflict derived from relational state. The corpus explicitly warned that the mathematical ordering/lattice structure should remain open. Sigma is a historical epistemic-state-vector formulation with five named dimensions. Its status as the ontological decomposition of F4 K_t is not established.
rows.statement: Names Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) historically as the 'Epistemic State Vector' with a Cartesian-product domain, then reports an adversarial audit finding that its five dimensions are not homogeneous semantic axes but rather span distinct roles (epistemic support, acquisition/provenance, lifecycle/resolution, temporal validity, and relationally-derived conflict), warning against treating Sigma as a proven ontological decomposition of F4's K_t.

rows.anchor: an epistemic requirement is not necessarily a factual proposition. So the corpus does not support treating r automatically as: proposition; truth claim; constraint; predicate; test; Boolean condition. It is a requirement object whose standard expresses what counts as satisfaction. MD-061 then narrows it to r=(component_r,Accept_r). That is a new candidate type, not the historical general requirement type. The semantic type of r is therefore not the same as the MD-061 r type.
rows.statement: Enumerates six candidate semantic categories the corpus explicitly does NOT support automatically applying to r (proposition, truth claim, constraint, predicate, test, Boolean condition), and explicitly distinguishes the corpus-native general requirement type from MD-061's narrower (component_r, Accept_r) candidate type as genuinely different types.

rows.anchor: MD-060 falsified the strong semantic-core hypothesis that all K_t variants are mutually information-preserving translations. The concrete counterexample was the incompatibility between the probabilistic V1/V3 family and categorical V7 fields. But that does not prove V7 is wrong. It proves that V1/V3 <-> V7 cannot be treated as automatically equivalent.
rows.statement: Reports MD-060's falsification of the strong semantic-core hypothesis (that all 12 K_t variants are mutually information-preserving translations of each other) via a concrete counterexample: the probabilistic V1/V3 family is incompatible with V7's categorical fields, proving only that V1/V3<->V7 cannot be assumed automatically equivalent, not that V7 itself is wrong.

rows.anchor: What would falsify Sat* specifically? A corpus observation could falsify it if the corpus supplied a case where the proposed rule predicts Sat*=1 while the independently established semantic requirement status is unsatisfied -- or vice versa. ... if a source explicitly established an ordering or relational rule among the five values that changes the acceptance semantics, MD-061's deliberate flat-set interpretation could fail. MD-061 did not find such a counterexample. But it explicitly refuses to interpret that absence as proof. V7/Sat* is falsifiable in principle. No corpus observation currently falsifies it. No corpus observation currently validates it either. That is exactly why it remains Gate C.
rows.statement: Specifies concrete falsification criteria for MD-061's Sat* construction (a corpus case where predicted Sat* disagrees with an independently established satisfaction status, or an explicit ordering/relational rule among the five Sigma values contradicting the flat-set interpretation), concluding Sat* is falsifiable in principle but currently neither falsified nor validated -- precisely why it remains Gate C.

rows.anchor: the missing corpus information has two layers: Layer 1 -- requirement semantics: for each requirement r, the corpus must establish what its acceptance standard means; standard exists historically, but standard -> Accept_r does not. Layer 2 -- state semantics: the corpus must establish which information in K_t determines that standard; MD-061 currently has this only for the V7 Sigma slice, and even there it is an explicit construction choice. The minimum missing fact is not simply 'more fields.' It is a corpus-grounded rule connecting a requirement's acceptance standard to the semantically relevant state information, such that satisfaction is determined without an additional modelling choice.
rows.statement: Decomposes the minimum missing semantic information into two explicit layers (Layer 1: requirement acceptance-standard semantics; Layer 2: which K_t state information determines that standard), concluding the missing fact is not simply more typed fields but a corpus-grounded connecting rule requiring no additional modelling choice -- consistent with but more explicitly layered than document6's 'Requirement-Evaluation Semantic Boundary' finding.

rows.anchor: We are currently doing both -- and must not confuse them. What we are reconstructing: K_t in K-blackboard, EC_t=EC(S_t,G_t,Q_t,C_t), Sat(K_t,EC_t), Delta_t={r in Req(EC_t): not Sat(K_t,r)} -- genuine historical semantic constructs, classified by MD-061 as corpus facts with the Delta shape frozen. What we are designing: V7 as the computational substrate, Req_Sigma, Accept_r, and Sat*(K_t,r)=1 iff pi_component_r(Sigma_t(K_t)) in Accept_r -- not recovered corpus semantics, a controlled candidate construction. MD-061 itself says: Not A: Sat* required this phase's own construction. Not B: three substantive modelling choices were required. Gate C -- CONDITIONAL CANDIDATE.
rows.statement: Consolidates the reconstructing-vs-designing distinction with an explicit corpus-facts list (K_t, EC_t, Sat(K_t,EC_t), Delta_t) versus a designed-constructs list (V7, Req_Sigma, Accept_r, Sat*), quoting MD-061's own self-adjudication (Not A, Not B, Gate C Conditional Candidate) verbatim.

rows.anchor: We have reconstructed the existence and role of F4's semantic satisfaction machinery, but we have not reconstructed its complete operational semantics. And MD-061's Sat* is a controlled candidate implementation of one possible semantics, not the recovered F4 semantics.
rows.statement: States the file's core conclusion distinguishing reconstruction of F4's satisfaction machinery's existence/role from reconstruction of its complete operational semantics, with Sat* explicitly labeled a controlled candidate implementation of one possible semantics rather than recovered F4 semantics.

rows.anchor: The resulting epistemic boundary (17-row status table): Does corpus contain Sat? YES-CORPUS FACT. Does corpus establish satisfaction/adequacy meaning? YES conceptually. Does corpus establish component-membership semantics? NO. Does corpus contain Accept_r? NO. Does corpus contain Req(EC_t)? YES. Does corpus contain Req_Sigma? NO-MD-061 narrowing. Is V7 established as F4's semantic model? NO. Is V7 the best-typed available candidate? YES. Are cross-variant same-state identities established? NO. Is Sigma=(A,S,R,V,C) historically defined? YES. Is Sigma proven ontological F4 decomposition? NO. Is Delta_t^Sigma mechanically computable? YES conditionally. Is full Delta_t computable? NO. Is Sat* corpus-native? NO. Is Sat* falsified? NO. Is Sat* validated as F4 semantics? NO. Is F3<->F4 mapping established? NO. The corpus contains an F4 semantic skeleton, not a recovered complete F4 operational semantics.
rows.statement: Consolidates the entire MD-060/MD-061 audit into a comprehensive seventeen-item yes/no status table, concluding the corpus contains an F4 semantic skeleton but not a recovered complete F4 operational semantics.

rows.anchor: Do not ask 'how do we implement the existing F4 Sat?' as though its semantics were already known. Ask first which parts of Sat are corpus-native and which parts would necessarily be a new semantic construction. That distinction is now directly demonstrated by MD-061 itself. No canonical V7, no canonical Accept_r, no canonical Req_Sigma, no F3<->F4 bridge, and no GA-001/GA-038 work follows from this result. The firewall remains intact.
rows.statement: Issues a critical correction to how any future research prompt should be framed: never assume F4 Sat's semantics are already known; first classify which parts are corpus-native versus necessarily new construction, reaffirming no canonicalization, no F3<->F4 bridge, and no GA-001/GA-038 progress follows from this audit.

rows.anchor: We are not yet reconstructing a complete existing F4 semantics. We are reconstructing the corpus-native shell of F4 and, where the corpus becomes semantically incomplete, constructing controlled candidates to discover exactly what is missing. MD-059 already found that the corpus contains the shape of K_t, Delta_t, R_t/requirements and Sat, but not the semantic instantiation needed to compute them. MD-061 then crossed that boundary deliberately: it constructed Sat* for one narrow V7 slice. Its own final classification is Gate C -- Conditional Candidate, explicitly not corpus-native.
rows.statement: States the executive framing that the research is simultaneously reconstructing the corpus-native F4 shell and, where incomplete, deliberately constructing controlled candidates; identifies MD-061's Sat* (built over a narrow V7 slice) as self-classified Gate C 'Conditional Candidate', explicitly not corpus-native, crossing the reconstruction/construction boundary deliberately.

rows.anchor: Sat exists [CORPUS]; Sat participates in Delta [CORPUS]; Sat is Boolean in the frozen formulation [CORPUS]; Sat means 'component membership in an accepted domain' [PROP]/MD-061 construction; Sat is generally an acceptance predicate Not established. Sat*(K_t,r)=1 iff pi_component_r(Sigma_t(K_t)) in Accept_r is MD-061's construction. MD-061 explicitly says Sat* is not corpus-computable and required substantive modelling choices.
rows.statement: Gives a precise per-claim provenance table for Sat, isolating exactly which parts are corpus-native (existence, role in Delta, Boolean codomain in the frozen formula) versus MD-061's own construction (the component-membership-in-accepted-domain interpretation, formalized as Sat*(K_t,r)=1 iff pi_component_r(Sigma_t(K_t)) in Accept_r).

rows.anchor: Accept_r comes from MD-061. I found no corpus-grounded definition establishing an Accept_r object. MD-061 defines r=(component_r,Accept_r) and then uses membership in Accept_r. The source provides the enumerated value domains of Sigma_t, but it does not say: for each requirement r, there is an acceptance domain Accept_r. Accept_r is constructed, not recovered.
rows.statement: Traces Accept_r to MD-061's own construction rather than the corpus: while the corpus provides Sigma_t's enumerated value domains, it never states that each requirement r has an associated acceptance domain Accept_r, so the mapping r -> Accept_r is a modelling decision, not a recovered fact.

rows.anchor: Req_Sigma was created by MD-061 as a restriction. The corpus gives Req(EC_t) inside the frozen Delta_t definition. But MD-061 introduces Req_Sigma subseteq Req(EC_t) as the subtype consisting of requirements that can be expressed using the five Sigma_t fields. The artifact itself calls this one of the three non-corpus assumptions required to make Sat* computable. Req_Sigma = the subset of requirements we chose to make computable over Sigma_t.
rows.statement: Establishes Req_Sigma as an MD-061-introduced restriction of the corpus's Req(EC_t) to only those requirements expressible via the five Sigma_t fields, explicitly one of three named non-corpus assumptions, distinguishing it sharply from 'the F4 requirements' in general.

rows.anchor: M0125 gives a typed Sigma_t=(A,S,R,V,C) substructure. That proves the fields and their enumerated domains occur in the corpus. It does not establish Requirement<->A or Requirement<->S etc, nor that an F4 requirement has the form (component, acceptableValues). MD-061 selected V7 precisely because Sigma_t was the only typed component in the 12-variant census. That makes it the best available construction substrate, not necessarily the F4 semantic model.
rows.statement: Clarifies that Sigma_t's typed fields (from M0125) prove only that those fields and domains occur in the corpus, not that individual requirements correspond to individual Sigma_t fields, or that requirements generally have a (component, acceptableValues) form; V7 was selected purely for typing-completeness (the only typed component among 12 K_t variants), not for semantic primacy.

rows.anchor: V7 = best currently constructible typed representation, not V7 = the canonical semantic F4 state. Indeed, V4b was textually closer to Sat's own definition but completely untyped, so constructing Sat over it would have required inventing the domains.
rows.statement: Sharply distinguishes 'V7 is the best currently constructible typed representation' from 'V7 is the canonical semantic F4 state' (the latter unproven), noting the rival variant V4b was textually closer to Sat's own definition but entirely untyped, so V7 was chosen for typing-completeness rather than closeness to Sat's intended meaning.

rows.anchor: MD-060 found 12 distinct formulations and explicitly concluded there was no corpus-internal, non-arbitrary way to select one canonical K_t. MD-061 reports: 'Same intended state' is not corpus-defined across variants. Current answer: Same semantic state across representations: OPEN. Representation equivalence relation: OPEN.
rows.statement: Cites MD-060's finding of 12 distinct K_t formulations with no corpus-internal non-arbitrary selection rule, and MD-061's finding that 'same intended state' is itself not corpus-defined across variants, leaving both cross-representation semantic identity (K^V7 equiv_sem K^V4b) and the representation-equivalence relation itself explicitly OPEN.

rows.anchor: The corpus does not currently fix its internal type [of r]... whether r is a proposition, predicate, constraint, obligation, test, condition, specification, acceptance criterion, or some composite object. MD-061 solved this locally by defining r=(component_r,Accept_r). But that is precisely the modelling choice under examination. Type(r)=OPEN and consequently Semantics(Sat)=OPEN until the type of r is established.
rows.statement: Enumerates nine candidate semantic categories for what a requirement r might denote (proposition/predicate/constraint/obligation/test/condition/specification/acceptance-criterion/composite), none fixed by the corpus, concluding Type(r) is OPEN and therefore Semantics(Sat) is OPEN until r's type is established -- MD-061's own r=(component,Accept) definition is itself flagged as the very modelling choice under examination, not a resolution.

rows.anchor: K_t = abstract epistemic state is corpus-supported. But TruthSource(K_t)=? remains OPEN. This is crucial because Sat could mean very different things depending on the answer: Sat_empirical versus Sat_logical versus Sat_normative versus Sat_contractual.
rows.statement: Identifies TruthSource(K_t) -- whether K_t is directly observed, a world reconstruction, a physical/probabilistic/normative state, or a verified truth-state -- as unresolved, and argues this matters decisively because Sat's meaning would differ across empirical/logical/normative/contractual interpretations depending on the answer.

rows.anchor: Computable Delta^Sigma != Validated Delta^Sigma. MD-061's T8 searched the relevant corpus for a worked example of Sat over Sigma_t and found none. The absence was explicitly not interpreted as evidence of correctness. To independently validate Delta_t, we need an external-to-the-computation criterion that establishes whether a requirement really is satisfied/unsatisfied.
rows.statement: Draws the distinction between a mechanically computable Delta^Sigma (under MD-061's three assumptions) and a validated Delta^Sigma, noting MD-061's own search (T8) for a worked corpus example of Sat over Sigma_t found none, and explicitly refusing to interpret that absence as evidence of correctness.

rows.anchor: F-V7-1 A primary F4 source explicitly assigns semantic meaning to K_t that cannot be represented by V7. F-V7-2 A primary F4 requirement refers to distinctions that V7 cannot represent. F-V7-3 Two V7 states identical under Sigma_t are explicitly distinguished by the corpus as different F4 states. F-V7-4 A primary source gives Sat semantics inconsistent with set-membership over the V7 domains. F-V7-5 A second independently sourced K_t representation is shown semantically equivalent to V7 while requiring distinctions V7 cannot preserve. That would directly attack the interpretation rather than merely attack the implementation.
rows.statement: Proposes a five-item falsification programme (F-V7-1 through F-V7-5) for testing whether V7 is the intended F4 semantic model rather than merely an internally-coherent, counterexample-free construction, each criterion specifying a concrete corpus observation that would directly attack the V7 interpretation itself.

rows.anchor: F3's outputs reached atoms; F4's outputs satisfied requirements; no corpus bridge exists between those types. F3 atom -/-> F4 requirement until an evidence-grounded mapping is found. And importantly, choosing V7 would not solve this problem. It would merely give us one F4 representation against which we could attempt the mapping.
rows.statement: Reaffirms the atoms-vs-requirements type mismatch between F3 and F4 (matching handover_verdict's N/O findings) and explicitly argues that resolving the V7-vs-canonical-K_t question would not by itself solve the F3<->F4 bridging problem -- it would only supply one candidate representation against which the still-missing mapping could be attempted.

rows.anchor: L0 -- Corpus-native F4: what the historical corpus actually says. L1 -- Corpus-derived semantic consequences: what follows formally from L0 without substantive semantic invention. L2 -- Constructed semantic candidate: what we introduce so that the system becomes executable/testable. K_t in K-blackboard: L0; Delta_t formula: L0; Sat(K_t,r) exists as dependency: L0; Sigma_t=(A,S,R,V,C) in V7: L0; Sigma_t typed domains: L0; Req_Sigma: L2; Accept_r: L2; r=(component,Accept): L2; Sat* membership rule: L2; Delta_t^Sigma: L2 computation; V7 equiv canonical F4: NOT ESTABLISHED; K^V7 equiv K^V4b: OPEN; F3 atom <-> F4 requirement: OPEN.
rows.statement: Introduces a reusable three-layer classification (L0 corpus-native, L1 corpus-derived consequences, L2 constructed candidates) and classifies every current F4 object into it, explicitly designed to prevent 'best computable construction' from silently being mistaken for 'recovered semantics'.

rows.anchor: There is a later derived verification artifact that claimed K=(A,R) with Assertion=(id,P,e,c,t,Pi) and even called the minimality result proven. That does not resolve the F4 questions. It belongs to the derived verification/reduction work, not the corpus-native Model-B F4 semantic lineage. The F4 audit explicitly says cross-corpus semantic infrastructure must not be silently relabelled F4 semantics. So we should not use that K=(A,R) result to answer 'what is F4 K_t?'
rows.statement: Explicitly warns against using the separately-derived verification-lane K=(A,R)/Assertion result (matching the Carrier-C kernel work from carrier-options/S2878 in this same batch) to answer the F4 K_t question, naming this exact substitution as the kind of cross-corpus semantic relabeling the F4 audit forbids.

rows.anchor: Before any further construction, every proposed F4 semantic object must be classified as either [CORPUS], [DERIVED], or [CONSTRUCTED]. F4 semantics are not yet reconstructed in full. What has been reconstructed is the semantic boundary: the corpus gives us the shell (K_t, Req, Sat, Delta_t), but not the closed semantics that make the shell executable. The more fundamental research question is now: Can the corpus itself determine the type of r and the semantic relation between K_t and r? If the answer is no, then F4 is not merely incompletely typed; its satisfaction semantics are underdetermined by the corpus.
rows.statement: Issues a governance gate requiring every proposed F4 semantic object be classified [CORPUS]/[DERIVED]/[CONSTRUCTED] before further construction, and reframes the central open research question as whether the corpus itself can determine Type(r) and the K_t-r relation -- a negative answer would demonstrate F4's satisfaction semantics are underdetermined by the corpus, not merely incompletely typed.

rows.anchor: the research has now moved from 'discovering that semantic primitives exist' to 'proving that they compose into a computable, cross-comparable semantic kernel.' I would sharpen the seven gaps like this: 1. EC_t->Sat OPEN/primary blocker; 2. Requirement type OPEN; 3. K_t typing OPEN; 4. F3<->F4 OPEN/independent blocker; 5. equiv_sem OPEN/foundational; 6. F1/F5/F6/K0 NOT STARTED; 7. GA-001/GA-038 OPEN.
rows.statement: Reframes the research programme's status via seven explicit, ranked gaps with status labels, characterizing the current phase as having moved from primitive-discovery to needing to prove those primitives compose into a computable, cross-comparable semantic kernel.

rows.anchor: Accept_r should not currently be treated as a discovered corpus primitive. The corpus gives us satisfaction/adequacy language, but the construction of Accept_r and the interpretation of Sat* as component-membership were introduced in the research process rather than established by the corpus. That makes your #1 even sharper.
rows.statement: Corrects any treatment of Accept_r as a discovered corpus primitive, reaffirming (consistent with document4/S2894) that Accept_r and the component-membership interpretation of Sat* were introduced during the research process, sharpening gap #1 (EC_t->Sat).

rows.anchor: The real bottleneck is #1+#2. At present we effectively have K_t, EC_t, r but not the missing semantic function (K_t,r,EC_t) -> Sat(K_t,r,EC_t). More specifically, we need something like EC_t -> Standard_r -> AcceptanceCondition_r -> Sat(K_t,r), with every arrow supported by corpus evidence or explicitly marked as a research proposal. Without that, we cannot legitimately compute Delta_t = {r in Req_t: not Sat(K_t,r)}. And without Delta_t, the whole Zero/adequacy machinery remains underdetermined.
rows.statement: Identifies the combined bottleneck (gaps #1+#2) as the missing semantic function (K_t,r,EC_t)->Sat, decomposed into a required four-stage chain EC_t -> Standard_r -> AcceptanceCondition_r -> Sat(K_t,r), arguing that without it Delta_t cannot be legitimately computed and the entire Zero/adequacy machinery remains underdetermined.

rows.anchor: field typing != semantic typing. A tuple can have a datatype and still have no defined epistemic semantics. What is missing is something closer to [[K_t]] with each component having: carrier/type, allowed values, semantic interpretation, relations to other components, temporal behavior, status/uncertainty behavior, role in satisfaction. That is why V7 is currently best understood as a computational substrate, not yet the established F4 semantic model.
rows.statement: Sharpens gap #3 by distinguishing field typing from semantic typing (a tuple can have a datatype yet no epistemic semantics), specifying seven required semantic-typing dimensions per K_t component (carrier/type, allowed values, semantic interpretation, inter-component relations, temporal behavior, status/uncertainty behavior, role in satisfaction), reinforcing V7's status as computational substrate rather than established semantic model.

rows.anchor: Even if tomorrow we solved Sat(K_t,r) we still would not automatically have F3<->F4. We would still need a structure-preserving correspondence Atoms_F3 <-> Requirements_F4, including the semantics of what an atom contributes to requirement satisfaction. Solving the first does not solve the second. F4 internal semantics (EC->Standard->Accept->Sat, typed K_t) and F3<->F4 (atom->requirement correspondence) are two separate problems.
rows.statement: Argues gap #4 (F3<->F4 bridging) is genuinely independent of gap #1/#2 (F4 internal semantics): solving Sat would not automatically produce the required structure-preserving Atoms_F3<->Requirements_F4 correspondence, since these are two separate problems with distinct dependency trees.

rows.anchor: We currently have three competing notions of semantic equivalence: weak observation-shaped approx_obs; M0043 behavior-based equivalence; KR-CONTR-FDE's total-identity form. They cannot simply coexist as though they were different notations for the same thing. This matters enormously because the kernel definition currently depends on equiv_sem. Our frozen minimality formulation is MinKer(C_KOS) = Min_{<=_sem}{K in K_adm: K |= C_KOS}. If equiv_sem is unsettled, then the equivalence classes themselves are unsettled. Therefore Kernel minimality cannot yet be adjudicated. That is not a failure of the kernel research. It is the correct consequence of the dependency structure.
rows.statement: Names three genuinely incompatible historical candidates for semantic equivalence (weak observation-shaped approx_obs, M0043 behavior-based equivalence, KR-CONTR-FDE's total-identity form) and derives a direct consequence for kernel research: since the frozen minimality formula MinKer(C_KOS)=Min_{<=_sem}{K in K_adm: K|=C_KOS} depends on equiv_sem, and equiv_sem is unsettled among three incompatible candidates, kernel minimality cannot currently be adjudicated -- framed as a correct consequence of the dependency structure, not a failure of kernel research.

rows.anchor: the census is close to complete, but the theory is still at its very first, narrow, unvalidated foothold is accurate. The corpus has discovered many candidate structures. But semantic instantiation means we can actually write something like F_i: X_i -> Y_i and specify what X_i, Y_i, admissibility, interpretation, transformation and satisfaction mean. Until that happens, an F1/F5/F6/K0 entry is essentially a research placeholder.
rows.statement: Endorses the characterization that the candidate census is nearly complete while the theory itself remains at a narrow, unvalidated foothold, clarifying that true semantic instantiation requires fully specified functions F_i:X_i->Y_i with admissibility/interpretation/transformation/satisfaction semantics -- absent that, F1/F5/F6/K0 remain research placeholders.

rows.anchor: GA-001 and GA-038 are not merely two remaining questions sitting at the end of a checklist. They are currently blocked research questions. Requirement semantics -> [Sat/Accept, Typed K_t] -> F3<->F4 -> equiv_sem reconciliation -> [F1, F5, F6/K0] -> GA-001/038 -> Kernel selection -> Stage 07 formalization. The exact dependency edges still need to be audited, but the direction is right.
rows.statement: Gives a full eight-stage dependency graph from requirement semantics through Sat/typed-K_t, F3<->F4 bridging, equiv_sem reconciliation, F1/F5/F6/K0 instantiation, GA-001/GA-038, kernel selection, and finally Stage 07 formalization, explicitly flagging GA-001/GA-038 as currently blocked research questions rather than checklist items nearly complete.

rows.anchor: Given this status, I would not: select a kernel; add more kernel operators; declare Sat computable; promote Accept_r; declare V7 to be the F4 model; choose one equiv_sem merely because it is convenient; start Stage 07 formalization; write Theory v1.3; interpret the recent Zoom/biological/Linga work as solving these gaps. That would violate the evidence boundary.
rows.statement: Lists nine specific actions explicitly forbidden given the current evidence state (selecting a kernel, adding operators, declaring Sat computable, promoting Accept_r, declaring V7 canonical, choosing equiv_sem by convenience, starting Stage 07, writing Theory v1.3, or treating unrelated Zoom/biological/Linga work as solving these gaps), each framed as a violation of the evidence boundary.

rows.anchor: Corpus discovery [checkmark] != Semantic closure. Semantic closure != Kernel minimality. Kernel minimality != Implementation. So the project is not at 'kernel engineering.' It is at: constructing and validating the semantic bridge that would make a kernel comparison meaningful. In one sentence: The census has largely told us what candidates exist; the next research must establish what those candidates mean, how they compose, and under what formally defined conditions one semantic state satisfies another. That is the real frontier now.
rows.statement: States three chained non-identities (Corpus discovery != Semantic closure != Kernel minimality != Implementation) positioning the project's true current stage as constructing and validating the semantic bridge that would make kernel comparison meaningful, not kernel engineering itself, and names this the real research frontier.

rows.anchor: None of A-D is exactly correct. The dependency chain in the mission, T -> R_req -> EvaluationRepresentation -> TypedBoundary -> OutcomeSpace -> Contr -> Sat, contains one important error: The corpus does not establish that T determines R_req. The mandatory operation universe T and the requirement universe R_req are related in one historical proposal, but that relationship was never closed as a corpus-grounded implication.
rows.statement: Rejects the mission's proposed seven-stage dependency chain (T -> R_req -> EvaluationRepresentation -> TypedBoundary -> OutcomeSpace -> Contr -> Sat) by identifying that its first implication (T determines R_req) is never corpus-established, only related in one historical proposal.

rows.anchor: More importantly, the immediate blocker for computing a semantically faithful Sat(K_t,r) is neither T nor the choice of an outcome codomain. It is: the missing semantic interpretation of a requirement r -- especially the boundary connecting EC_t to its acceptance conditions. I would name this the: Requirement-Evaluation Semantic Boundary. It is the hardest unresolved object.
rows.statement: Names the true immediate blocker as the 'Requirement-Evaluation Semantic Boundary' -- the missing semantic interpretation connecting a requirement r and its epistemic contract EC_t to concrete acceptance conditions -- explicitly distinguishing it from both the operation universe T and the outcome codomain choice, either of which had previously been treated as the primary blocker.

rows.anchor: The corpus never closes the semantic path: EC_t -> Req(EC_t) -> r -> AcceptanceCondition(r,EC_t,...) -> Sat(K_t,r). That missing middle is exactly what MD-062 exposed. MD-062 reconstructed the surrogate and found: the requirement shape r=(component_r,Accept_r) never takes EC_t as an argument. And: EpistemicContract and AcceptanceCondition are different bounded contexts with no stated connection. This is the strongest result in the whole audit. Therefore EC_t -/-> AcceptanceCondition has not been established.
rows.statement: Reports MD-062's decisive negative finding: MD-061's requirement shape r=(component_r, Accept_r) never actually takes EC_t as an argument, and EpistemicContract and AcceptanceCondition are separate bounded contexts (in the DDD sense) with no stated connection between them -- called the strongest result in the entire audit series, establishing that EC_t does not reach AcceptanceCondition.

lineage_claims.target: document4.md/S2894's account of MD-061's Sat* and Accept_r construction, same batch
lineage_claims.quote: the requirement shape r=(component_r,Accept_r) never takes EC_t as an argument

rows.anchor: Without that connection, we cannot know what the requirement actually asks Sat to evaluate. This is why the problem is not simply 'we need a better evaluator.' We first need to know what the evaluator is supposed to evaluate.
rows.statement: Argues that the missing EC_t->AcceptanceCondition connection means the problem is not merely needing a better Sat evaluator, but not yet knowing what the evaluator is even supposed to evaluate.

rows.anchor: The sibling Contr experiment (M0127) independently reinforces this: M0127 tested flat evaluation representations and found that bare values lose distinctions. The structured representation retained Standing + Boundary where the boundary included Reason/Provenance/Context/Condition. Value alone =/= Sufficient semantic evaluation. But we must not jump from that to Sat = Standing+Boundary. That would violate the corpus firewall.
rows.statement: Cites M0127's Contr experiment as independent corroboration that bare/flat values lose necessary distinctions (a structured Standing+Boundary representation with Reason/Provenance/Context/Condition was required instead), explicitly warning against jumping from this corroboration to defining Sat as Standing+Boundary, which would violate the corpus firewall.

rows.anchor: The outcome space is relatively easy syntactically: Sat(K_t,r) in {0,1}. That shape is explicitly present in the historical corpus. But the semantic meaning of those values is not closed. Codomain known syntactically != evaluation semantics known. The difficult object is the pre-codomain semantic boundary.
rows.statement: Corrects a proposed diagnostic option (C) by distinguishing codomain-known-syntactically from evaluation-semantics-known: the {0,1} shape is easy and already present, but the actual difficulty lies entirely in the pre-codomain semantic boundary (what a requirement even means), not in choosing the outcome codomain.

rows.anchor: T subseteq O is present, but no rule says which operations are MANDATORY. It also records that no operation had a semantic body, identity, or ratification in that reconstruction. T is not corpus-fixed as a mandatory universe. T unresolved =/=> Sat cannot be locally constructed. MD-061 already constructed a restricted Sat* without closing T. So T is an upstream foundational dependency for broader semantic sufficiency/minimality, but it is not the immediate cause of the current Sat semantic failure.
rows.statement: Separates T's unresolved mandatory-membership status from the immediate Sat blocker: although T is not corpus-fixed as a mandatory operation universe, MD-061 already demonstrated constructing a restricted Sat* without closing T, so T's unresolved status is an upstream dependency for broader minimality claims but not the proximate cause of Sat's current semantic failure.

rows.anchor: R_req is not corpus-fixed as a mandatory normative contract. The historical requirement document calls itself [PROPOSED RATIFICATION] despite the filename containing RATIFIED. The later audit explicitly found [RATIFIED] stamps in research material but no locatable governance acts for R_req/SPEC-RREQ. That is a governance fact about the current evidence, not a judgement about legitimacy. But R_req has already yielded real mathematical results: 11 conditions, 12 required distinction pairs, graph-colouring formulation, minimum flat-domain size as chromatic number of that tested required-distinction graph. tested R_req != universally ratified R_req.
rows.statement: Finds R_req self-described as [PROPOSED RATIFICATION] despite a filename containing 'RATIFIED', with [RATIFIED] stamps present but no locatable governance act -- a governance-evidence gap, not a legitimacy judgement -- while still crediting R_req with genuine tested mathematical results (11 conditions, 12 distinction pairs, a graph-colouring formulation with chromatic-number-based minimum flat-domain size), explicitly distinguishing tested R_req from universally ratified R_req.

rows.anchor: Factivity does NOT block Contr. It is a parallel decision track. And the later F4 Sat* audit found that the immediate failure was not a factivity counterexample; it was missing distinctions and missing contract semantics. Factivity != immediate Sat bottleneck. It remains essential to the eventual semantics of Knows, but it does not tell us what Sat(K_t,r) means.
rows.statement: Corrects the ordering of the factivity result (Knows(a,p,c,t)=>True(p,c,t) unsatisfiable for an attributive total Gamma when truth is absent, 420 violations in 10,000 cases) relative to Sat: factivity does not block Contr and is not the immediate Sat bottleneck, remaining essential only to the eventual semantics of Knows.

rows.anchor: Contr(p,K) iff Pos(p,K) and Neg(p,K) was shown to be necessary but insufficient because retraction and supersession are not necessarily current contradiction. Also, a candidate representation could satisfy the existing invariants while mapping contradiction to Satisfied, exposing a missing distinction. Therefore Contr remains [EXP][OPEN] and cannot currently be selected as the final evaluation component. But this does not prevent identifying the current Sat bottleneck.
rows.statement: Restates that Contr(p,K) iff Pos(p,K) and Neg(p,K) is necessary but insufficient (retraction/supersession are not necessarily current contradiction, and a candidate representation could satisfy existing invariants while mapping contradiction to Satisfied), keeping Contr as [EXP][OPEN] without this blocking identification of the Sat bottleneck.

rows.anchor: Delta_t shape is settled enough to use historically. What cannot yet be done is evaluate its members. So Delta_t is not the bottleneck. Sat is. equiv_sem is not required to diagnose the present Sat bottleneck. It becomes essential when we ask whether a future Sat is representation-independent.
rows.statement: Clarifies Delta_t's frozen shape is settled enough to use historically (not itself the bottleneck; only member-evaluation is blocked by Sat), and that equiv_sem, while still formally open, is not required to diagnose the present Sat bottleneck -- it only becomes essential later when asking whether a future Sat is representation-independent.

rows.anchor: The exact dependency picture should therefore be corrected: Epistemic Contract EC_t -> Requirement Instance r -> [MISSING SEMANTIC BRIDGE] -> Acceptance/Evaluation Boundary Semantics -> [K_t semantics, Boundary metadata (reason/context/provenance/condition)] -> Sat -> Delta_t -> Zero/Gap. Separately: T -> required distinctions/operational sufficiency -> relevant to R_req completeness; R_req -> representation preservation -> Contr/evaluation/Zero requirements. But the corpus does not establish a closed arrow T => R_req.
rows.statement: Provides a corrected dependency diagram placing the missing semantic bridge explicitly between Requirement Instance r and Acceptance/Evaluation Boundary Semantics (feeding into K_t semantics and boundary metadata before Sat and Delta_t), while keeping T and R_req as a separate, only loosely related branch with no closed T=>R_req arrow.

rows.anchor: Hardest unresolved object: Requirement Interpretation / Evaluation Boundary. Not merely Sat. More precisely: The corpus has a requirement object and a satisfaction predicate, but has not defined the semantic interpretation that maps an instantiated requirement under an epistemic contract to the distinctions, evidence, context, provenance, temporal conditions, and acceptance conditions that Sat must evaluate against K_t. In DDD language: EpistemicContract -/-> AcceptanceCondition is the missing domain relationship.
rows.statement: States the audit's headline conclusion for the research ledger: the hardest unresolved object is Requirement Interpretation/Evaluation Boundary, not Sat itself, formalized in DDD terms as the missing domain relationship EpistemicContract -/-> AcceptanceCondition.

rows.anchor: Because Sat is supposed to answer Sat(K_t,r)? But unless we know what r means, we don't know what information from K_t is relevant. Suppose type=temporal. What must Sat inspect? current timestamp? validity interval? transition history? source freshness? temporal dependency? context? an external temporal model? The corpus contains pieces of all these concepts, but does not provide the semantic rule connecting them. That is why adding ten more fields to K_t would be premature.
rows.statement: Worked example (a temporal-type requirement) showing seven candidate inputs Sat might need to inspect (timestamp, validity interval, transition history, source freshness, temporal dependency, context, external temporal model) with no corpus rule selecting among them, arguing this is why extending K_t with more typed fields would be premature before the semantic rule exists.

rows.anchor: A T not fixed [TRUE, but not the immediate Sat blocker]. B T fixed -> incomplete R_req [UNSUPPORTED]. C T,R_req fixed -> evaluator type is blocker [TOO LATE/INCORRECT]. D enough material to define Sat without modelling choice [REFUTED]. A is independently true; D is false; B is unestablished; C misses the actual semantic bottleneck.
rows.statement: Formally adjudicates four candidate diagnostic hypotheses about the F4 research state: A (T not fixed) true but not the immediate blocker; B (T fixed implies incomplete R_req) unsupported; C (evaluator-type is the blocker once T/R_req fixed) too late/incorrect since neither is fixed and a harder problem precedes codomain choice; D (enough material exists to define Sat without a modelling choice) refuted by MD-062.

rows.anchor: I would not ask for a governance ratification of T yet, and I would not extend Sigma_t to the remaining ten components. The corpus's own latest hard-stop says the smallest next action is: incorporate EC_t, or a Reason/Provenance/Context-style boundary channel, into the requirement/Sat construction before further component typing. Authorize a narrow research act to reconstruct the corpus-grounded EC_t -> r -> AcceptanceCondition boundary. Not to define Sat. The act should answer only: What semantic information does the corpus require a requirement instance to carry, and how does EC_t determine which acceptance conditions apply, before any evaluator or outcome codomain is chosen?
rows.statement: Recommends one precisely scoped next research act -- reconstructing the corpus-grounded EC_t -> r -> AcceptanceCondition boundary, explicitly not defining Sat itself -- while ruling out two premature alternatives (ratifying T, or extending Sigma_t to its remaining ten components), framed as the smallest action attacking the actual bottleneck.
