sources.note: The synthesis track's continuous governance ledger itself, as a first-class object: 96 numbered entries (GN-01..GN-96) recording every HPA ruling, gate, commission, and finding-disposition in the book-production and theory-verification programme from 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-02, with its own internal renumbering-collision discipline (a later label colliding with an already-used GN number is recorded under a fresh number with the collision noted, never silently renumbered).

rows.anchor: Generated synthesis artifacts must never become evidence for the historical corpus from which they were derived
rows.statement: GN-01 (HPA-accepted, 2026-08-28): a provenance feedback-loop rule -- any file in the corpus that is content-identical to a synthesis artifact is classified SYNTHESIS-ECHO and carries zero evidential weight, formalized as E_historical intersect E_synthesis-derived = empty set, adopted after discovering a synthesis status report had been saved verbatim back into the source corpus. GN-02..GN-07 (2026-08-28) record the standing decisions of the earliest phase: Phase 1 archaeology complete/validation open; Phase 2A delivered; Phase 2B authorized then accepted; a new evidence category SUPPORTED-BY-COMPOSITION (all links individually verified, composition assembled by review -- stronger than hypothesis, weaker than ESTABLISHED); Lord-naming decision reserved to HPA; PQ-02 weighting sharpened so the analytic unit is a reasoning lineage/artifact chain, not a clock hour; corpus-statistics discipline generalized as a standing rule that all corpus statistics are time-stamped observations, never timeless properties.

rows.anchor: The Constitutional status formula (binding for all later artifacts incl. the book): the architecture is architecturally coherent and substantially evidence-supported; formal synthesis and implementation conformance remain to be established -- never validated.
rows.statement: GN-08..GN-13 (2026-08-28, Phase 2D acceptance and book planning): Phase 2D accepted with GAP-1/GAP-2 closures graded (CLOSED-BY-COMPOSITION / CLOSED); Omega ruled to belong to theory/history rather than the final ubiquitous language; the constitutional-status formula adopted (coherent and evidence-supported, never 'validated'); the central architectural thesis adopted as working thesis (KnowledgeOS is an architecture for moving from partial observation to warranted state, decision and authorized action under an explicit purpose and epistemic contract, not primarily a storage architecture); a book principle that the book must show how the architecture became discoverable, not a clean-story rewrite; Phase 3 authorized progressively (3A now, 3B/3C/3D later); Phase 3B falsification delivered with four defects F-1..F-4 found and none yet applied.

rows.anchor: No sentence in the final book may silently upgrade the epistemic status of the underlying evidence.
rows.statement: GN-14..GN-18 (2026-08-28, book planning): a constitutional book rule that no sentence may silently upgrade the epistemic status of underlying evidence; book structure decided in form (folder-per-chapter, each with chapter.md + evidence-map.md + claims.md + unresolved.md) but deferred in content -- chapter titles are illustrative, not canonical, until after 3B repairs and 3C complete; the book organizing principle fixed as organized around the reconstructed architecture, never one-folder-per-source-session and never around session chronology, with the discovery journey told through the architecture's structure rather than as a transcript.

rows.anchor: ACCEPT F-1, F-2, F-3, F-4. ... The ruling authorizes application of exactly R-1..R-4 to v0.1; no other architectural change is authorized.
rows.statement: GN-19's history is itself a recorded governance error and its correction: an initial GN-19 entry recorded ACCEPT F-1..F-4 as an executed HPA ruling, but the source message was in fact a hedged recommendation, not a ruling -- the synthesis engineer had applied repairs on that basis, violating the discipline finding != proposed repair != authorized repair. The error was recorded, not hidden: GN-19 was re-graded PROVISIONAL and canonical-architecture-v0.2.md re-graded PREPARED-UNRATIFIED until the explicit HPA ruling arrived, which then ACCEPTED all four repairs (F-1 governed/versioned policy-change route via DC+BC_Governance; F-2 with the specific resolution of adopting Zero(K,EC) as canonical while retaining Zero(K,G,EC) as historical lineage; F-3 epistemic ladder Candidate->Supported->Accepted with Committed re-typed as a decision-boundary status under A6; F-4 covering-relation/no-skip axiom) and produced canonical-architecture-v0.2.md as the current authorized model, with v0.1 retained unmodified as the pre-falsification record.

rows.anchor: The book gate does NOT open immediately after 3C. Formal sequence: 3B -> repair ruling (done) -> apply repairs v0.1->v0.2 -> 3C repository conformance -> BRAINSTORMING ARCHAEOLOGY ... -> FINAL ARCHITECTURE freeze -> book architecture -> book.
rows.statement: GN-20 (sequence amendment, confirmed 2026-08-28, later relabelled GN-21 due to a numbering collision the ledger records rather than silently renumbers): fixes the formal governance sequence 3B -> repair ruling -> apply v0.2 -> 3C conformance -> Brainstorming Archaeology -> Final Architecture freeze -> book architecture -> book, with the rationale that the book must not become authoritative around an architecture that later changes because an important historical brainstorming artifact surfaces. GN-21/22 authorize 3C planning then execution against v0.2 under a nine-constraint scope-and-evidence-plan discipline (five-verdict vocabulary CONFORMANT/PARTIALLY CONFORMANT/NON-CONFORMANT/NOT ESTABLISHED/OUT OF SCOPE, no silent upgrade of NOT ESTABLISHED).

rows.anchor: CF-001 -- resolve-before-Final-Architecture; CF-003 -- resolve-before-Final-Architecture; CF-006/CF-009 -- feed-into-Final-Architecture; CF-010 -- adjudicate
rows.statement: GN-23/24 (2026-08-28): 3C conformance findings accepted with no finding dispositioned yet, interposing Gate A (findings disposition) before Gate B (Brainstorming Archaeology authorization); Gate A's HPA ruling assigns CF-001 (authority/ownership of the divergent kos-v11-ddd Reference Architecture v1.1 worktree) and CF-003 (Constitution v1.0's in-force/ratified status) to resolve-before-Final-Architecture, CF-006/CF-009 (repository epistemic-state vocabulary) to feed-into-Final-Architecture, and CF-010 (a CSV/EXP-01-record discrepancy) to adjudicate -- restating that disposition != repair != resolution != architectural change. GN-25 adds a standing rule that prompt-delivery artifacts saved into the historical corpus are classified PROCESS/PROMPT, never archaeological evidence, unless a later ruling explicitly includes them.

rows.anchor: resolve CF-001 and CF-003, adjudicate CF-010
rows.statement: GN-26 authorizes the Brainstorming Archaeology phase only, binding the GN-25 prompt-artifact rule and a fixed classification vocabulary (HISTORICAL-FACT/-HYPOTHESIS/-EXPERIMENT/-DECISION/-ALTERNATIVE/-OPEN-QUESTION/-ABANDONED/-SUPERSEDED/PROCESS-PROMPT-ARTIFACT/DUPLICATE-DERIVATIVE/UNCLASSIFIED) and a v0.2-mapping vocabulary (CONTRIBUTED/SUPPORTS/EXPLAINS EVOLUTION/SUPERSEDED/CONTRADICTS/UNRESOLVED/NO CURRENT CORRESPONDENCE) that never says 'therefore v0.2 is correct/wrong'. GN-27 executes the ruling: CF-001 resolved (the kos-v11-ddd worktree is an unmerged parallel authorized branch, main branch remains programme-authoritative, RA v1.1 becomes a named Final-Architecture intake-or-scope-out input); CF-003 resolved (Constitution v1.0 WAS ratified via a retrospective ratification record, the PROPOSED banner is a stale defect only); CF-010 adjudicated (the prose verdict document prevails; the CSV is unreliable-without-its-generator). GN-28 handles a second, post-completion Gate B authorization per the standing duplicate-instruction discipline: only genuine deltas executed, nothing re-run.

rows.anchor: Phase authorization only ... Baseline: v0.2 authorized; GN-19/24/27 stand; archaeology outputs are historical evidence, never authority
rows.statement: GN-29 authorizes the Final Architecture phase with seven mandatory inputs (A-G, incl. RA v1.1 intake decision, three kernel traditions reconciled/layered/scoped-apart/unresolved never silently selected, Atma-Kernel explicit disposition) and fifteen governance rules including no silent v0.2 modification and mandatory [E]/[IN]/[RC]/[H]/[R]/[U] grading; the 'validated' vocabulary remains forbidden. GN-30 prepares (without ruling) the FA-9 ratification packet: the proposal equation v0.2 + D-FA-1..7 + OQ-1..12 = PROPOSED Final Architecture, with an HPA ruling template of per-determination ACCEPT/AMEND/DEFER.

rows.anchor: The HPA ratified the proposed Final Architecture as presented in FA-9: D-FA-1..D-FA-7 all ACCEPT.
rows.statement: GN-31: HPA ratifies the Final Architecture -- D-FA-1 layered state model unchanged; D-FA-2 RA v1.1 kept as a parallel lane, intake deferred; D-FA-3 the three Zero senses remain distinct, no merge authorized; D-FA-4 kernel traditions layered, object-level membership left OPEN; D-FA-5 Atma-Kernel an explicitly unresolved lens with no architectural role; D-FA-6 a qualified K_t naming register, no silent conflation; D-FA-7 OQ-1..OQ-12 remain OPEN/DEFERRED exactly as ratified, their unresolved status being PART OF the ratified architecture, never accidental incompleteness. Riders OQ-10 and OQ-6 held (not executed). Book Architecture and Book explicitly NOT authorized by this ruling -- a separate BOOK ARCHITECTURE AUTHORIZATION act is required.

rows.anchor: AUTHORIZE per BA-0 as presented, without amendment. DESIGN ONLY ... BA-1...BA-6 RATIFIED as presented
rows.statement: GN-32/33/34: the Book Architecture Authorization packet (BA-0) is prepared (not ruled), then the design-only Book Architecture phase is authorized (GN-33: chapter architecture, mappings, content allocation, provenance/terminology/verification architecture -- explicitly not chapter prose or production), then BA-1..BA-6 are ratified as presented (GN-34), subordinate to and conformant with the ratified Final Architecture; book production itself remains a separate, not-yet-authorized next gate.

rows.anchor: Book Production ... 25 chapters (Part III first, then I, II, IV) ... Status: BOOK PRODUCED -- DONE-PENDING-REVIEW.
rows.statement: GN-35: HPA authorizes Book Production (Authority order: ratified FA, then ratified Book Architecture, then archaeology as evidence/narrative only), with placement derived via php scripts/doc-placement.php to docs/knowledgeos/reviews/synthesis/book/; explicitly excludes any v0.2/FA/BA modification, sense-merges, kernel crowning, or Lord/Atma resolution. Execution complete the same day: 25 chapters produced (Part III first) each with chapter/evidence-map/claims/unresolved artifacts, plus a book index and provenance index; four book-level gates (structure conformance, provenance-index 100% resolution, Part III [FA]-claim traceability, forbidden-vocabulary sweep) all PASS. Status: BOOK PRODUCED -- DONE-PENDING-REVIEW, next act reserved for a separate BOOK REVIEW/ACCEPTANCE ruling.

rows.anchor: An HPA-relayed instruction arrived directing preparation of a Book Production Authorization packet ... asserting a baseline of "Book production: NOT AUTHORIZED" ... the asserted baseline contradicts the authoritative record
rows.statement: GN-36: a stale, out-of-sequence gate-preparation instruction (evidently authored before the GN-35 ruling was issued, asserting book production was NOT authorized when GN-35 already authorized and executed it) is detected against the record rather than blindly followed; per the standing defect rule ('if something is defective, STOP and report it -- do not fix a governance defect silently'), nothing is created or rewound, and two disposition options (confirm the standing record, or an explicit rewind ruling) are put to the HPA with no default assumed -- the first instance of a recurring duplicate/stale-instruction discipline later invoked again at GN-73/GN-87.

rows.anchor: Verdict: PASS WITH OBSERVATIONS ... GN-38: Ruling: Option B. ... An independent review of at least dimensions B, D, H is commissioned
rows.statement: GN-37/38/39/40/41: the book review-acceptance packet reports PASS WITH OBSERVATIONS (self-review, disclosed) but stops short of acceptance; HPA commissions an independent fresh-context reviewer (GN-38) who finds four localized defects D-1..D-4 (an over-attributed VALIDATED/QUESTIONABLE list, two altered ratified grade annotations in III.10, an unsupported timing specificity, a mechanical Lord-token failure) plus ten observations, none structural (GN-39); D-1..D-4 are then corrected under strict scope (D-2 by exact byte-verbatim restoration) and freshly re-verified clean (GN-40); the HPA then rules ACCEPT the corrected book (GN-41), explicitly noting book acceptance has no architectural effect on OQ-1..12/riders/RA v1.1, and that the synthesis programme's gate chain GN-01..GN-41 is complete through book acceptance.

rows.anchor: Decision 1 -- BA AMENDMENT: APPROVED ... Decision 2 -- EDITION 2 PRODUCTION: APPROVED. Order: Part III -> Part II -> Part IV -> the evidence-ready Part I chapters
rows.statement: GN-42: Edition 2 commissioned as a deeper, full-depth technical book atop the frozen/accepted Edition 1 (which stays FROZEN/ACCEPTED as a reference edition, never rewritten retrospectively): a BA amendment approved requiring substantive sections, worked examples, and no upgrading of an open proposition into architectural fact; production order Part III -> Part II -> Part IV -> Part I; kernel research (I.3) approved as a separate evidence commission awaiting a 38-document evidence base rather than inference; master constraint: Edition 2 may explain the architecture more deeply but may not expand it merely because deeper explanation creates theoretical gaps.

rows.anchor: Taxonomy AF-1..AF-10: contradiction, undefined dependency, compression loss, boundary violation, layer leakage, authority leakage, evidence-grade inflation, missing transition semantics, circularity, implementation impossibility.
rows.statement: GN-43 adopts a Book-Driven Architecture Verification Protocol for Edition-2 production: every chapter carries parallel exposition and verification outputs, checked against a ten-item architecture-flaw taxonomy AF-1..AF-10, with findings recorded outside the book's authority in a dedicated architecture-findings register (AF-F-n) and an explicit rule that the book-production agent may discover/classify/report findings but may not resolve them without a separate governance act. GN-44: the commissioned hostile pass over Edition-2 III.1-III.8 plus a cross-chapter chain test over Knower->G->IdealState->EC->K_t->Zero->Evidence->Admission->Decision->Authorization->Action->K_{t+1} reports CHAIN COHERENT WITH FINDINGS (no contradiction inside the taught architecture, 17 candidate findings AF-F-7..23 recorded, one BLOCKING) and identifies a systemic pattern: 'states, structures and boundaries were formalized; transformations and identities between them were not.'

rows.anchor: Book-side findings: bounded correction AUTHORIZED ... only demonstrable book errors; no architecture modification ... III.9: PROCEED
rows.statement: GN-45: a four-part findings disposition authorizes bounded book-only corrections for ten specific findings while explicitly deferring two (AF-F-8: may an [IN]-graded ratified framing be taught at bare [FA]?; AF-F-17: an authority-internal OQ-label collision untouchable by book correction) as governance questions; routes the compression-family findings (PF-1/5/6/7/8/9 + AF-F-9/11) to a formal mathematical audit (GN-46); rules III.9 may PROCEED provided it explicitly teaches the findings affecting kernel subject matter without silently resolving them, restating the principle that the book exposes issues while governance controls their disposition.

rows.anchor: Verdicts: architecture boundary/invariant layer MATHEMATICALLY SOUND WITH QUALIFICATIONS ... formal-object layer MATHEMATICALLY UNDER-SPECIFIED ... 22 findings MV-F-1..22 (12 MEDIUM, 5 LOW, 5 OBSERVATIONS, zero CRITICAL/HIGH)
rows.statement: GN-46/47: an independent mathematical/statistical/computational verification track is commissioned and delivers a 627-line report plus reference implementations. Verdicts: the invariant layer is mathematically sound with qualifications (the one invalidity, I-9's 'four-way' claim, is descriptive not normative); the formal-object layer is under-specified (signatures without constructions); computable under restrictions, not computationally realized; the EXP-01 historical verdict is independently reproduced and its negative conclusion confirmed and shown provable (no scalar can retain (S+,S-)); the CSV discrepancy is mechanically explained as mixed raw/pipeline semantics. 22 findings recorded, zero CRITICAL/HIGH; one positive finding that binary Zero(K,EC) is directly source-attested, so R-2's evidential basis is stronger than the ruling recorded. Nine recommended governance actions logged, none executed.

rows.anchor: 2 ARCHITECTURAL DEFECTS (both wording-level) ... 4 ARCHITECTURAL CANDIDATES ... Final verdict: COHERENT WITH QUALIFICATIONS. Edition-2 production can safely continue
rows.statement: GN-48/49/50: all 48 register entries (PF-1..9, AF-F-7..23, MV-F-1..22) are classified into 27 underlying findings across a fixed seven-way disposition vocabulary (2 architectural defects, 4 architectural candidates, a research set, 8 intentional compressions, 7 mathematical clarifications, book-only items, false-positives); GN-49 determines MV-F-6 (a flow-edge typing concern) is a MODELLING OMISSION (unstated lift d:=adopt(a)), not a genuine type error, and reaches final verdict COHERENT WITH QUALIFICATIONS -- production can continue, architectural closure awaits R1 (transformation semantics)/R2 (identity calculus)/R3 (evidence-calculus successor) research. GN-50 accepts the disposition, corrects the governing formulation to 'no demonstrated contradiction or invariant violation; several formal under-specifications remain,' adopts R1/R2/R3 as the consolidated research register, and adds a standing rule (BA-ED2-11) that every major formal relation in Edition-2 chapters is represented in a relation-status table so no relation looks more complete than it is.

rows.anchor: Part III PASSES WITH CORRECTIONS REQUIRED ... Method verdict: ADJUSTED -- seven named adjustments
rows.statement: GN-51..GN-54: a Part III Method & Quality Gate integrates hostile architectural verification, mathematical/statistical checks, provenance verification, and cross-chapter consistency; GN-52 adopts a supervision model (Edition 1 provides the narrative backbone, Edition 2 the reconstructed intellectual depth, RED/AMBER/GREEN criticism tiers, and the governing instinct 'smoothness must never consume truth'); GN-53 reports Part III PASSES WITH CORRECTIONS REQUIRED (all book-side, no BLOCKING finding) and an ADJUSTED method verdict (seven adjustments including a claim-strength inheritance check added at GN-54: a compressed summary/table/diagram must never carry stronger epistemic status than the passage it summarizes); GN-54 accepts the gate, authorizes and executes the corrections, and releases Part II production under the adjusted method.

rows.anchor: Part II Production Started ... II.1 RED HOLD TRACED -- FILE INTACT; DELIVERY-BOUNDARY FINDING AF-F-30 ... RED HOLD RELEASED; II.1 GREEN
rows.statement: GN-55..GN-64: Part II (II.1-II.4) is produced and reviewed chapter by chapter under the strict historical-epistemic separation (SOURCE RECORD -> HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION -> LATER INTERPRETATION -> CURRENT RATIFIED UNDERSTANDING). A false-alarm episode (GN-56/57) traces a suspected II.1 RED finding to a delivery-boundary corruption (the producer's condensed chat rendition, not the authoritative file, which verifies intact by md5) rather than a content defect, prompting a new binding production control (BA-ED2-13: verbatim machine-emitted file content + md5, never a condensed rendition). Subsequent chapters (II.2 DDD-lens review GN-58/59; II.3 three-lens audit GN-60/61 finding two RED wrong-attribution defects; II.4 GN-62/63/64) each go through AMBER-audit-then-correction-then-GREEN cycles, adding BA-ED2-14 (citation-content substantiation) as a binding control.

rows.anchor: PART II ACCEPTED. Scope of that acceptance ... the governed synthesis as a book Part and its evidential discipline -- not the completeness, establishment, or proof of the mathematical theory.
rows.statement: GN-65..GN-70: a whole-Part Part II Review Gate (independent hostile review across seven dimensions) reports PASS WITH CORRECTIONS (ten RED, nine AMBER findings, all wording/citation/apparatus-level); all corrections are applied and re-verified clean (GN-67); a further independent Final Acceptance Review reading II.1-II.4 as one argument reports ACCEPT WITH CORRECTIONS (one RED reintroduced by the correction pass itself, owned as a producer lapse); GN-70 closes Part II acceptance, explicitly stating book acceptance is not acceptance of the theory, and that OQ-1..12/riders/RA v1.1/DDD-F-1..8 all remain untouched by the acceptance.

rows.anchor: From this point the book session's role is book-production governance and controlled synchronization only. No new KnowledgeOS theory investigation is begun here
rows.statement: GN-71: standing lane-separation constraints fixed for the book session -- BOOK records research history and evidential status, THEORY RESEARCH discovers/verifies, INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION challenges prior conclusions, ARCHITECTURE determines implications, GOVERNANCE authorizes decisions, never substituted for one another; a five-way change-classification gate (editorial/evidence/structure/theory/governance) requires STOP-and-authorize for theory or governance changes; explicitly notes an independent verification session is separately investigating whether the KnowledgeOS theory's apparent closure is justified, and that synchronization with that report is deferred.

rows.anchor: Book Readiness / Synchronization Audit ... is the book ready to RECEIVE an independently verified theory report without contaminating the historical record or silently upgrading claims? ... BOOK LANE STATUS: READY WITH CONDITIONS
rows.statement: GN-72: a book-readiness audit (not a theory investigation) sweeps all 14 produced chapters for premature theory-closure language (zero occurrences of 'theory is complete/closed/established'), audits every OQ's treatment status, confirms no evidence-class upgrade has occurred anywhere (I-11/I-12 never carried toward TESTED), and drafts a Part IV entry contract and a Theory-to-Book Synchronization Gate (ten entry conditions, a freeze rule for mid-production theory arrivals) requiring HPA adoption before Part IV begins. Verdict: book lane READY WITH CONDITIONS; no book changes required now.

rows.anchor: An Independent Theory Verifier mandate ... was issued to THIS session. Held pending HPA decision ... Conflict 3 -- the mandate's central premise is superseded (decisive).
rows.statement: GN-73: a class-4 (theory) mandate addressed to the book session is held rather than executed, citing three conflicts -- it contradicts GN-71's own standing lane restriction issued one turn earlier; its independence premise is false for this session (which authored v0.1/v0.2/the book and cannot independently verify its own model, per the engineering-never-accepts-its-own-work rule R-34); and its central premise (that the theory was verdicted 'CLOSED') is already superseded by newer verification-lane artifacts recording 'STRUCTURALLY OPEN AND SEMANTICALLY OPEN -- the prior closed hypothesis is FALSIFIED' and eight separate verdicts (3 RED, 5 PARTIAL). Also flags a material collision for HPA attention: the policy-change loop was closed twice, differently, by two unreconciled resolutions of one problem (ratified I-11+R-1 vs a 2026-08-30 audit) -- an ES-005.4 violation.

rows.anchor: THE DECISIVE FINDING -- the two lanes do not share a vocabulary. Measured over root B's governed artifacts ... A, R, Sigma, Q_t, O, Provenance, Replay, Measurement = 0 occurrences each.
rows.statement: GN-74/75: a phase-transition mandate commissions a Theory-to-Book Canonical State registry assembled from three independent read-only extractions (~240 verification artifacts); the decisive finding is that the ratified book/architecture lane and the verification-research lane share almost no vocabulary -- measured over the ratified surface, A (assertion set), R (relations), Sigma, Q_t, O (operations), Provenance, Replay and Measurement each occur 0 times, and the ratified K_t is a different object from the verification lane's K=(A,R); exactly one construct (Policy) carries an explicit governance act. Also flags a structural conflict (GN-74): a proposed new 12-chapter Part III collides with the already-produced, already-gated 10-chapter ratified Part III, so no Part III/IV prose may be written until the HPA rules on structure. GN-75 additionally registers self-attested authority strings in the research track ('Authority: HPA' x13, 'HPA Ruling' x9, 'RATIFIED' x2) with zero ledger counterparts.

rows.anchor: the ratified v0.2 names ZERO operations (grep = 0) ... objects (partial), state, invariants, operations BLOCKED, transformations BLOCKED, evidence (partial), governance (GC-1 open), software/tests (narrow, 16/25 unobserved)
rows.statement: GN-76/77: a book-structure-crosswalk proposal identifies a decisive implementation gap -- the ratified v0.2 plus FA-1..FA-9 contain zero operation definitions and zero pre/postcondition specifications anywhere in the ratified record (independently verified: exactly one non-operation hit for pre/postcondition language, the word 'postcondition' occurs zero times); nine capabilities are canonically REQUIRED while zero operations are canonically DEFINED, and of 99 contract cells (9 capabilities x 11 properties) only 2 are fully fixed by canon and 88 are empty. Sharpest formulation: the ratified canon defines when a transition would be ILLEGAL without ever defining what a transition IS. Three components identified as necessary to close the gap: a closed operation registry with a membership criterion, typed rejection/failure semantics, and a state identity+equality rule.

rows.anchor: A ratification cannot presently be signed on evidence ... Part B four signable options -- 1 COMMISSION the derivation ... 2 RATIFY a named candidate ... 3 RULE OPEN ... 4 DEFER
rows.statement: GN-78: a draft (unsigned, non-authoritative) HPA ruling instrument for the operation registry is prepared, reporting rather than resolving three obstacles to ratification -- at least three non-agreeing candidate membership lists exist, none governed; the necessity/minimality criterion has never been executed by anyone; the leading candidate's own latest artifact states it must NOT be frozen as-is. Four signable options offered (commission the derivation, ratify a named candidate, rule open/blocked, defer), with an eight-point acceptance standard for any future registry.

rows.anchor: HPA ruling, explicit and unhedged: Option 1 -- commission the derivation. ... commissions the ARCHITECTURE/THEORY lane to derive a canonical operation registry fit for ratification
rows.statement: GN-79/80: HPA selects Option 1, commissioning a four-task derivation (membership+closure claim; execute the never-before-performed minimality/necessity test; reconcile two operations unreconciled against the executed algebra; an eleven-field per-operation contract) bound by an eight-point acceptance standard C-1..C-8, explicitly not ratifying, adopting, or resolving GC-1/I-11/Sigma/Q_t/identity/equality/replay/measurement/aggregation. GN-80 sets the executor route: an independent fresh-context agent derives, a different fresh-context agent reviews, and the book session itself commissions/records/assembles rather than deriving -- preserving GN-71's lane separation without a lane change.

rows.anchor: AC-6 (the HPA's specific watch item) -- the mandatory-capability set must be shown entailed by the RATIFIED canon, not imported from the research lane's view of what KnowledgeOS should do.
rows.statement: GN-81/82: acceptance checks AC-1..AC-6 fixed as binding on the derivation before it lands -- candidate-universe completeness, minimality actually executed (a described test is a failed test), no hidden dependence on unratified constructs, alternatives reported not selected by preference, reviewer genuine independence, and AC-6 (entailment scrutiny: every claimed-mandatory capability must trace to a ratified object/invariant/governance rule, never 'the theory needs it'). GN-82 adds AC-0, an ordering rule preceding every gate: evaluate whether the derivation earned the right to propose its registry before evaluating whether the registry 'makes sense.' Verdict C (no minimal registry establishable) and verdict B (multiple minimal registries, implying the remaining question is normative not mathematical) are both recorded as valid, non-failure outcomes.

rows.anchor: Recommended terminal verdict: D -- THE OPERATION UNIVERSE DEPENDS ON AN UNRESOLVED PRIOR CANONICAL DECISION ... 57 distinct live names / 17 sources ... 6 minimal registries in each of three requirement variants
rows.statement: GN-83/84: the commissioned derivation delivers, recommending (not ratifying) terminal verdict D -- the operation universe depends on unresolved prior canonical decisions, foremost the typing of Reject. Headline computed results: 57 distinct candidate operation names from 17 sources with the intersection of thirteen claiming enumerations EMPTY; a mandatory-capability set R_A=15; six minimal registries found across three requirement variants (band invariant at 9); Reject appears in the core of all six as the only operation reaching the ratified REJECTED state, yet I-12 is violated by Split and Reject, and Article 8 is violated by Reject. GN-84's HPA assessment fixes a permanent terminology distinction -- 'minimal under the chosen computational criterion' is NOT 'minimal canonical operation set of KnowledgeOS'; the first is shown non-unique, the second has not been demonstrated at all -- and elevates three findings (AF-F-31 the Reject/I-12/Art.8 tension; AF-F-32 a witnessed A6 crossing; AF-F-33 a prior bound that is PROPOSED not DERIVED) so they cannot be lost.

rows.anchor: The evidence chain is genuinely replayable ... AC-1 FAIL ... FALSIFIED: (i) the stated ground for verdict D ... (ii) the candidate universe ... (iii) the I-12 bypass discovery ... (iv) op_Replay does not replay ... COMMISSION COMPLETE -- STOPPED.
rows.statement: GN-85/86: acceptance procedure fixed in advance (a five-rung status ladder RATIFIED->FORMALLY DERIVED->COMPUTATIONALLY VERIFIED->PROPOSED->OPEN, a named forbidden path 'the six candidates are good enough -- choose the most sensible one'); the independent falsification pass then partially survives and partially falsifies the derivation -- AC-1 (candidate-universe completeness) FAILS outright (a 24-operation table missed, ~19 names in neither list, three later steps uncited); the stated ground for verdict D is re-characterised from inconsistency to underdetermination (op_Reject implements no source-status guard to violate); the I-12 bypass finding is traced to a hardcoded return-rung in the derivation's own script rather than a real architecture gap; op_Replay is found to only set-and-test a flag rather than replay (the identical defect class used earlier to discredit a withdrawn witness); a Constitution clause (Art. 8.3, 'Resolution SHALL be forward-only') central to the return-rung question was never consulted by the derivation at all. Both lanes independently recommend verdict D, but on incompatible grounds; commission STOPPED, nothing ratified.

rows.anchor: The mandate requires independently written code. The completed reviewer wrote none ... THE OPERATION REGISTRY IS NOT VERIFIED.
rows.statement: GN-87: a falsification mandate arriving after the pass was already executed is handled as a gap analysis, not a re-run, per the standing duplicate-instruction discipline (a full re-run would duplicate ~2.5M tokens of completed work). Three genuine gaps found, one commissioner-caused (the independent review replicated rather than independently reconstructed the tests); the acceptance gate is determined regardless: since AC-1 (candidate-universe completeness) FAILED, 'THE OPERATION REGISTRY IS NOT VERIFIED' by the HPA's own pre-fixed rule, and no further pass can lift an AC-1 failure because completeness is a property of the candidate universe, not of the testing. Of the HPA's four possible outcomes, D obtains, with the ordering correction that a new prerequisite P-11 (what is the operation universe, and what act closes it?) is prior to all of P-1..P-10.

rows.anchor: resolve the preconditions that prevent a canonical operation algebra from being derived legitimately ... PRECONDITIONS -> DERIVE -> FALSIFY -> DECIDE -> RATIFY -> TRANSFORMATIONS -> IMPLEMENT -> TEST.
rows.statement: GN-88/89: Step 284 commissioned to resolve three precondition questions (P-11 operation-universe closure; P-1/AF-F-31 the Reject typing question; A6/Article 8.3 the evidence-authority boundary) via two independent read-only extractors, explicitly barred from repairing, choosing, or inferring any governance act. GN-89 fixes the output form in advance: deliverable 04 must be a seven-column dependency matrix (never a narrative), every finding must take the form 'Primary-text evidence establishes X. Therefore Y is constrained. The remaining decision is Z,' and P-11 is split into three distinct decisions (P-11a membership criterion, P-11b source-admissibility rule, P-11c the closure act) that must never be collapsed back into one.

rows.anchor: P-1 VERDICT: OPEN -- and the alleged conflict is NOT ACTUALLY A CONFLICT ... A6/Art. 8.3: no textual contradiction found ... THE CONSTITUTION'S OWN STATUS IS CONTRADICTORY.
rows.statement: GN-90: primary-text reconstruction finds the Reject/I-12/Art.8 tension (AF-F-31) is not actually a conflict, because the presupposed specification (256.11) explicitly denies being a specification twice in its own text ('Possible semantics', 'not yet an accepted mathematical specification'); reclassifies it as semantic underdetermination with a governance consequence, and finds three mutually incompatible typings of Reject plus one explicit refusal to type it. Finds A6/Article 8.3 has no textual contradiction and does not itself answer the return-rung question, and that the alleged 'I-12 bypass' is actually an Article-8 question about governed resolution, not an I-12 question -- two questions had been running together. Records a commissioner misattribution (a quote wrongly attributed to Reference Architecture v1.0, actually Constitution Article 11.3) as owned and corrected by the extractor. Discovers a new, prior-to-everything problem: the Constitution's own in-force status is contradictory across three records (its own PROPOSED/NON-AUTHORITATIVE banner; GN-27/CF-003's 'WAS ratified, stale banner only'; and the very instrument GN-27 cites, which itself says 'PRODUCED, PROPOSED').

rows.anchor: determine whether KnowledgeOS has a complete and traceable chain -- derivation -> definition -> formal establishment -> architecture -> governance -> implementation -> empirical observation -- and identify exactly where it breaks.
rows.statement: GN-91: Step 285 commissioned as a theory-chain-closure and canonicalization audit across five never-collapsed status dimensions (Derivation/Definition/Architecture/Governance/Implementation/Empirical), with a binding rule that RATIFIED may be inferred only from the GN ledger, FA ratification, or v0.2 authorization -- never from words like 'accepted,' 'final,' or a self-attested 'Authority: HPA' line. Carries forward the Constitution's contradictory status (from GN-90) as a named hard-stop condition so the eventual verdict cannot be written as though the ground under Articles 3/4/6/7/8/9/11 were settled.

rows.anchor: 48 distinct enumerations exist ... the intersection is EMPTY and executed ... v0.2 + FA-1..FA-9 contain 0 operations and 0 occurrences of the word operation ... step order and file order disagree
rows.statement: GN-92: the P-11 extraction finds the operation universe was never bounded at all (a stronger finding than AC-1's 'a table was missed') -- 48 distinct enumerations exist, their intersection is empty and their union is at least 100 names against a 57-name working set the derivation actually ranged over; v0.2+FA-1..FA-9 contain zero operations and zero occurrences of the word 'operation.' New findings AF-F-34 (two more compute-over-a-hand-table artifacts, one containing a loop that provably cannot fire), AF-F-35 (nine incompatible universe-boundary pairs, including one file containing both a closure claim and its own withdrawal under the same COMPLETED/Authority:HPA status line), and AF-F-36 (step numbering and file authorship order disagree in a range where a later document admits 'our later work jumped over that derivation' -- so 'later step number' is not sound evidence of supersession in that range).

rows.anchor: Sigma, Q_t, qualification = 0 occurrences across v0.2, v0.1 and FA-1..FA-9 ... Q_t binds THREE incompatible objects ... Sigma minimality is contradicted in the corpus and the reconciliation omits the refutation.
rows.statement: GN-93: the epistemic/governance extraction measures Sigma, Q_t and qualification at zero occurrences across the whole ratified surface (all NO ACT); Policy is found to be the only construct in the block with real governed architecture. Four new findings: AF-F-37 (Q_t binds three incompatible objects across the corpus, uncovered by any naming-collision register); AF-F-38 (a same-date corpus artifact refutes the Sigma-minimality-4 result the ratified chain relies on, and a later reconciliation document omits that refutation from its own table); AF-F-39 (Policy is placed both inside and outside K by different executed/ratified sources, one of which stands against v0.2's own wording); AF-F-40 (Sigma/Q_t independence holds only 'by mutual absence' -- the strong non-interference claim remains untested, the six counterexample constructions unrun).

rows.anchor: the programme does NOT need to return to derivation. The remaining work is definition -> architecture -> governance ... section 17 HARD STOP ACTIVE -- five of six conditions met.
rows.statement: GN-94: Step 285 completes with six assembled deliverables and answers the mandate's decisive question -- derivations exist in abundance, what is missing is a decision admitting any of them, including deciding between competing same-date derivations (Sigma 3-vs-4 values, two opposite identity repairs, Policy inside-vs-outside K). Five completeness conclusions are recorded, never merged: derivation substantial-but-non-uniform, definition weakest (at least 26 knowledge-state forms, state equality and Qualify's body absent outright), architecture small-and-mostly-constraints, governance exactly-one-construct-with-a-real-act (Policy), implementation-readiness a-static-state-with-nothing-that-changes-it. The chain is found to break precisely at definition->architecture and at operations (first broken edge) and again at identity/equality. A 21-item blocker register is produced (14 semantics-undefined, 4 implementable-not-claimable, 3 claimable-not-certifiable); the section-17 hard stop is declared ACTIVE with five of six trigger conditions met, and Step 285 stops there, repairing none of them.

rows.anchor: Recorded HPA framing: the programme now has an executable investigation capable of demonstrating non-uniqueness rather than merely asserting uncertainty
rows.statement: A recurring methodological principle recorded across the operation-registry commission (GN-85): a verification that confirms the underlying computation is correct but refuses to grant it canonical status is itself a SUCCESSFUL verification, not a failure -- 'the computational result is correct, but it does not establish canon' is an explicitly legitimate and expected outcome, distinguished from a verifier simply finding nothing wrong.

sources.note: Step 210 'Invariant Verification Matrix' (phase_measure_theory): proposes a 6-tuple V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i) per invariant (invariant/owner/enforcement/monitoring/test/failure-behavior) and produces a 15-row, 60-cell matrix with all cells filled (breaking the corpus's prior all-'?' placeholder pattern) but realizing only 3 of the 6 declared tuple components (Invariant/Owner/Verification-test-name); boxes 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' and 'Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity'. rows.anchor: each file's tail contains the agenda for the next step
rows.statement: Structural observation, load-bearing for the whole verification: each file in the 208-215 band ends with the agenda section for the *next* step (e.g. the file titled 'Step 208' ends with a '# Step 209' section at line 1423 onward), so the band is a chain of overlapping documents and every 'Step N' agenda exists in two places (as the prior file's tail and the next file's own opening).

rows.anchor: Cardinality drift: the 8-set I_KOS is silently superseded by a 15-list I1-I15 without amendment
rows.statement: Probe (c-iii): Step 209 Section 209.42 boxes and freezes an 8-member invariant set I_KOS = {I_identity, I_version, I_provenance, I_temporal, I_epistemic, I_authority, I_decision, I_execution}. Step 210 Section 210.25 then tabulates 15 invariants I1-I15 with no mapping given between the 8 and the 15. Independently checked: I13 (illegal transitions rejected) and I14 (preconditions/postconditions) have no member of I_KOS to belong to, and I15 (no semantic strengthening) is likewise unhoused unless forced into I_epistemic. The 8-set is silently superseded by the 15-list without amendment; only Step 209's own caveat ('we should not freeze this yet') prevents this from being an outright contradiction.

rows.anchor: POPULATED. 60 of 60 cells filled. ZERO '?', ZERO TBD. THE ALL-'?' PATTERN IS BROKEN.
rows.statement: Probe (d): Step 210's 15-row invariant-verification matrix (lines 809-825) has 60 of 60 cells filled with zero placeholders -- a real, material departure from the corpus's prior pattern (Steps 108, 112, 114, 116, 121 all used all-'?' matrices), credited as a genuine corpus-level improvement.

rows.anchor: The matrix realizes 3 of the 6 tuple components it is supposed to instantiate
rows.statement: Step 210 Section 210.1 boxes V_i = (I_i, O_i, E_i, M_i, T_i, F_i) (invariant, owner, enforcement mechanism, monitoring mechanism, test/verification, failure behaviour) but the rendered matrix has only 4 columns (ID, Invariant, Owner, Verification) realizing I_i, O_i, T_i -- E_i (enforcement), M_i (monitoring), and F_i (failure behaviour) are absent for all 15 invariants: 45 of the declared tuple components are unrealized. Enforcement is the one component that would distinguish an architectural property from an architectural principle, the exact distinction Step 210's own boxed opening claim rests on.

rows.anchor: The Verification column contains test NAMES, not test RESULTS
rows.statement: Step 210's Verification column lists 15 test names verbatim (identity transition test, version reconstruction, lineage traversal, semantic contract test, negative inference test, payload/semantic test, reproducibility test, privilege-path test, failure simulation, outcome verification, conflict test, historical replay, state-machine test, invariant test, transformation test) with zero results, zero of the fifteen tests existing as code, and none run (confirmed by Part 2's zero-executable-fences finding). Under TEST SPECIFIED != TEST EXECUTED: 15/15 specified, 0/15 executed.

rows.anchor: DDD CATEGORY ERROR IN THE 'Owner' COLUMN
rows.statement: Step 206 Section 206.15 derives the candidate bounded-context set as Observation, Evidence, Assessment, Governance, Decision, Execution. Step 210's Owner column instead contains values like 'Domain' (a layer), 'Persistence/Domain' (two layers), 'Knowledge infrastructure' (a layer), 'Assessment/Contracts' (half artifact-kind), 'Aggregate' (a tactical pattern, not a party), and 'Contracts' (an artifact kind). Only 4 of 15 invariants (I5, I7, I8, I12) have a single, named bounded-context owner; seven (I1, I2, I3, I11, I13, I14, I15) have an owner entirely outside the derived context set, making them ownerless invariants under Step 212's own Section 212.15 criterion; five (I2, I4, I6, I9, I10) have slash-shared owners, Step 212's own Section 212.16 shared-ownership problem.

rows.anchor: Step 210's matrix instantiates, in 12 of its 15 rows, the two failure modes Step 212 names two files later — and neither file notices
rows.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 warns explicitly against 'Ownerless Invariants' (I exists but Owner(I) = empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints the same 15 invariants from Step 210 with the Owner column deleted entirely, and performs no such search -- discarding the exact data (Step 210's Owner column, with 7/15 ownerless and 5/15 shared) that would have triggered Step 212's own diagnosis.

rows.anchor: Further arithmetic checks: 0.87>=0.80 correct; 0.91+/-0.08 within range at 1 sigma but 2-sigma bound exceeds 1; ratio checks disclaimed
rows.statement: Additional independently-verified arithmetic in the band: Step 209 Section 209.15's 0.87 >= 0.80 evaluates to True (correct). Step 208 Section 208.14 / Step 210 Section 210.12's 0.91 +/- 0.08 gives [0.83, 0.99], within [0,1] at 1-sigma, but at 2-sigma the upper bound is 1.07 > 1 -- out of range for a quantity called 'confidence', though the corpus never commits this specific error since the interval's coverage level is left unlabelled. Step 215 Section 215.24's ratios (182/43=4.233, 43/17=2.529, 17/8=2.125, 8/4=2.0, total 45.5x) make no arithmetic claim and are correctly disclaimed as unknown. Step 209 Section 209.42 vs Step 210 Section 210.25: |I_KOS|=8 vs |{I1..I15}|=15, difference 7, mapping absent (unreconciled).

rows.anchor: PREVIOUS DEPENDENCY: 1 (Step 208 only); LATER RESPONSE: Step 210 replaces I_KOS with I1-I15 without amendment
rows.statement: Step 209 cites exactly one prior step (Step 208) and zero prior invariant families. Later response in scope: Step 210 Section 210.25 replaces the 8-member I_KOS with a 15-row I1-I15 without amendment; Step 210 Section 210.9 restates Step 209's Section 209.25 semantic-strength principle as Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15.

rows.anchor: FORMAL OBJECTS: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i); Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity
rows.statement: Step 210 ('Invariant Verification Matrix') defines a 6-tuple V_i=(I_i,O_i,E_i,M_i,T_i,F_i) per invariant; boxes 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' and 'No claim of architectural compliance without identifiable evidence'; defines Reachable(D,E)!=empty; boxes 'Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity' and 'Epistemic state cannot be silently strengthened'; states Strength(T(x))>Strength(x) requires Justified(T); boxes 'Quantitative value without relevant uncertainty may constitute semantic loss'; defines a statistical-result 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity); boxes 'Documentation < ExecutableEvidence < FormalProof'; a conceptual Assurance(I)=f(Evidence,Coverage,Independence,Repeatability,Criticality); an E_1..E_5 evidence hierarchy (documentation..formal verification); the target for-all-s-in-S_reachable: I(s)=True; and boxes 'AI may assist assurance; AI should not be the sole source of assurance', plus the 15-row invariant-verification matrix itself (60/60 cells filled).

rows.anchor: LATER RESPONSE IN SCOPE: Step 211 reverses Test/Evidence order; Step 212 drops the Owner column and recalibrates E_n
rows.statement: Step 210 cites only Step 209 by number ('up to Step 209, we have asked...'). Later response: Step 211 Section 211.2 restates the assurance chain with Test before Evidence, contradicting Step 210's own Section 210.40; Step 212 Section 212.4 reprints I1-I15 minus the Owner column; Step 212 Section 212.6 re-mints an E_0..E_5 scale with different rung definitions than Step 210 Section 210.30's E_1..E_5.

rows.anchor: EVOLUTION/DEFINITION VERDICT: CLEAR on the principle/property distinction, CONTRADICTORY on E_1..E_5 (twice)
rows.statement: Step 210 answers 'where' (role names) and 'how proven' (test names) but not 'is it true' for any invariant. CLEAR: the principle/property distinction (its best contribution), Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity, the three assurance levels. INCOMPLETE: V_i is 6-ary, only 3 components ever instantiated. AMBIGUOUS: 'Owner' is used as bounded context, layer, pattern, and team interchangeably. CONTRADICTORY: E_1..E_5 vs Step 212's E_0..E_5 (Contradiction #3), and E_1 bound to two incompatible types within Step 210 itself (Contradiction #4: Section 210.20's evidence-item E_1 vs Section 210.30's documentation-rung E_1).

rows.anchor: FIRST INVALID INFERENCE: Section 210.30 vs 210.20 (E_n ambiguity); honest gaps in 210.26/210.28/210.29
rows.statement: Section 210.20 uses E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P as evidence items; Section 210.30, ten sections later, binds E_1=documentation...E_5=formal verification as evidence-strength levels -- the same subscripted symbol carries two incompatible types with no disambiguation, and every downstream use of E_n in Steps 212-214 inherits the ambiguity. Section 210.29 honestly declines to scalarize Assurance and names fake precision (Assurance=97.3%) as a hazard, yet Section 210.28 immediately prior writes Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I), a comparison requiring the very ordering Section 210.29 declines. Section 210.26 correctly concedes a test provides evidence, not proof (Test(I_8)=PASS does not prove I_8=True in all states), then Section 210.32's target for-all s in S_reachable: I(s)=True leaves S_reachable undetermined (Section 210.33 concedes this openly) -- an honest, correctly-labelled gap, not an invalidity.

rows.anchor: COMPUTABILITY: highest rung reached is INPUTS_KNOWN, for I_i/O_i as strings only; 15 tests specified, 0 run
rows.statement: V_i is DEFINED with 3/6 components at INPUTS_KNOWN (role-name granularity); the I1-I15 matrix is DEFINED->INPUTS_KNOWN (names) but not CONSTRUCTIBLE (no mechanism/code/test); Assurance(I) is DEFINED but explicitly barred from numeric evaluation; S_reachable is DEFINED but conceded as the open challenge, not CONSTRUCTIBLE. The highest rung reached anywhere in Step 210 is INPUTS_KNOWN, and only for I_i and O_i as strings. TEST VERDICT NOT_EXECUTED: 15 tests specified by name, 0 written, 0 run; Section 210.16's negative test ('can an AI-generated Assessment directly invoke an execution command? Expected: False') is designed in prose and never run against anything.

rows.anchor: STATISTICAL VERDICT: STRONG (the 8-tuple A=(theta-hat,...,Validity) is the best statistical section in the band); two correct refusals and two measurement violations
rows.statement: Section 210.13's 8-tuple statistical result A=(theta-hat,Estimator,Sample,Population,Model,Assumptions,Uncertainty,Validity) is correct and genuinely good statistical practice, rarely done in architecture documents, but never carried into the matrix (which collapses all eight back into one row) and never connected to the corpus's prior statistical steps (025N, 074, 082, uncited). Correct refusals: Section 210.29 declines to scalarize Assurance (names fake precision explicitly); Section 210.27's Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof is a properly-used ordinal. Violations: Section 210.28's Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I) compares assurance levels the same file declines to scale; the E_1<...<E_5 ladder (Section 210.30) is re-issued by Step 212 Section 212.6 with different rung contents and an added E_0 -- the same ordinal scale has two incompatible calibrations in the band, making any statement 'we have E_2 evidence' uninterpretable without knowing which file it was written under -- a scale-integrity failure that silently corrupts later aggregation. The 15-row matrix itself carries no scale at all (purely nominal, no arithmetic attempted -- correct).

rows.anchor: DDD VERDICT: MIXED — strong distinctions (Architectural Principle != Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Memory/Identity/History split), weak ownership
rows.statement: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property is exactly the right DDD-governance move; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity (Section 210.5, a foreign key proves existence not that this version was the artifact used) is a real and useful insight; Section 210.39's Memory/Identity/History separation, concluding the current domain object need not carry all history internally, is correct DDD (event sourcing / separate read model), well argued. Against this, the Owner column's category error means only 4/15 invariants have a single bounded-context owner, 7/15 are owned by a layer or pattern (which cannot be accountable), 5/15 are slash-shared, and I13/I14 are owned by 'Aggregate' -- a tactical pattern name is never the answer to 'who is accountable' in DDD.

rows.anchor: ASSUMPTIONS / HIDDEN ASSUMPTIONS / UNDEFINED SYMBOLS — Step 210
rows.statement: Stated: each invariant has exactly one owner; a test name determines a test; enforcement can be located by inspection. Hidden: that the 15 invariants are the right 15 (no derivation from I_KOS's 8, no completeness claim); that S_reachable is finite or tractable (required by the for-all quantifier, false for unbounded state); that Owner and Enforcement are separable -- the matrix drops Enforcement and keeps Owner, implicitly assuming Owner=Enforcement, which Step 211 Section 211.29 later denies ('Invariant->Owner present but Enforcement missing = a design gap'), meaning by Step 211's own criterion all 15 rows of Step 210's matrix are design gaps. Undefined symbols: Justified(T), Strength(x), Critical(I), HigherAssurance(I), Coverage/Independence/Repeatability, S_reachable, Estimator/Sample/Population/Validity, DA's codomain Result.

rows.anchor: WHAT SURVIVES / WHAT DOES NOT SURVIVE — Step 210, including the word 'Matrix' itself
rows.statement: Survives: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property; Referential Integrity < Semantic Historical Integrity; Documentation<ExecutableEvidence<FormalProof; the 8-component statistical result tuple; the refusal of test-as-proof; the refusal to scalarize assurance; the Memory/Identity/History split; the 15 invariant names as a working checklist. Does not survive: the Owner column (11/15 rows unusable); the Verification column as evidence of anything (0/15 executed); V_i as a realized 6-tuple (3/6 realized); E_1..E_5 as a stable scale; and the word 'Matrix' in the title -- a 4-column table realizing 3 of 6 declared dimensions, with no status and no results, is a checklist.

rows.anchor: The most damaging collision is E-binding #2 vs #5, which occurs INSIDE ONE FILE (Step 210)
rows.statement: Of the twelve distinct bindings of the glyph E catalogued across the band, the most damaging collision is internal to a single file: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P (an evidence item entailing a proposition), and Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (the weakest rung of an assurance ladder) -- same symbol, same file, incompatible types, no disambiguation, no notice.

rows.anchor: The symbol I is silently rebound between Step 208 (information measure) and Step 209 onward (invariant) with no announcement
rows.statement: Step 208 uses I exclusively for an information measure (I(E), I(A), I_required, I_preserved); Step 209 onward uses I exclusively for invariants (I_L, I_C, I_S, I_i, I_identity, I1-I15, I(s)). The rebinding is never announced -- a reader comparing I(C(A)) (Section 208.4, information) to I(s)=True (Section 210.32, an invariant predicate) is reading two different symbols under one glyph.

rows.anchor: The Evidence/Test ordering is reversed between files, and Step 210's own boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own tuple
rows.statement: Step 209's tail agenda for 210 orders Invariant->Owner->EnforcementPoint->Test->Evidence->FailureMode; Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple orders enforcement, monitoring, test, failure (test before the implied evidence); but Step 210's own boxed Section 210.40 conclusion states Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance (evidence before test); Step 211 Section 211.2 (boxed) and Step 214 Section 214.2 (boxed) both revert to Test before Evidence. Four sources agree that Test precedes Evidence; Step 210's one boxed conclusion disagrees with all of them, including with its own tuple -- the direction matters (Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test; Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout). This is Contradiction #5.

rows.anchor: Tuple arity drift: 'the ledger' alone is specified at five different arities across two files
rows.statement: Machine-tabulated arity drift across the band: V_i verification tuple is 6-ary (210.1) but realized at arity 3 in the matrix (210.25); AAG is previewed as a 5-tuple but delivered as a 2-part graph with 6 node classes (211.1); the assurance vector A is 6-ary (211.9) while an AI artifact A is 7-ary (211.21); I_KOS has 8 members (209.42) vs I1-I15 has 15 (210.25, 212.4); the ledger EL_i is specified at arity 10 (214.1), then 15 (214.6), then 8 (214 tail), then again at 8 and 20 columns in Step 215 (215.5, 215.29) -- five arities for one object ('the ledger') across two files. R(S_i) is 5-ary for 6 declared questions (215.1).

rows.anchor: A and Gap: eight bindings of A, four bindings of Gap with two different ordinal category sets
rows.statement: A denotes: Assessment (208-212, throughout), an aggregate state A_t (209.13), the architecture-as-CSP set A (209.34), an assurance vector (211.9), an AI-artifact 7-tuple (211.21), a statistical-result 8-tuple (210.13), an architecture snapshot A_t (213.16-18), and an artifact A_j (213.4) -- eight bindings, with Section 209.13's aggregate-state A_t formally indistinguishable in notation from Section 213.17-18's architecture-state A_t (delta(A_t,c)=A_{t+1} vs A_0->A_1->...). Gap denotes: a numeric difference (211.4, 212.10), an ordinal category (211.4's {None,Low,Medium,High,Critical} vs 212.10's different {None,Partial,Significant,Critical,Unknown}), a class (212.11 G1-G5), and a register row (212.31 G-01-G-15) -- four bindings, with the two ordinal category sets differing from each other.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #1 — Knowledge as a generic object: forbidden in 208, used as an Owner in 210
rows.statement: Step 208 Section 208.28 boxes a prohibition: the Data->Information->Evidence->Assessment->KnowledgeClaim transformations of semantic status 'should not [be collapsed] into one generic object called Knowledge.' Step 210 Section 210.25's matrix row I11 nonetheless assigns Owner='Knowledge' (and row I3 compounds it with 'Knowledge infrastructure'), the exact generic object Step 208 boxed a prohibition against two files earlier in the same band. Severity HIGH; neither Step-206 bounded context, and neither file notices.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #3 — The evidence-strength scale is recalibrated between Step 210 and Step 212
rows.statement: Step 210 Section 210.30 defines E_1=documentation, E_2=manual inspection, E_3=automated test, E_4=property-based test, E_5=formal verification. Step 212 Section 212.6 defines E_0=No evidence, E_1=Claim/documentation, E_2=Static implementation evidence, E_3=Executable test evidence, E_4=Runtime/production evidence, E_5=Formal verification. E_2, E_3 and E_4 disagree between the two files (only E_5 agrees), so a claim 'has E_4 evidence' means a property-based test under Step 210 and production observation under Step 212 -- entirely different assurance. Aggravating factor: Step 212's calibration silently matches the uncited Step 109's (E2=implementation, E4=runtime), so Step 212 restores an earlier convention without knowing it. Severity HIGH.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #4 — E_1 bound twice inside Step 210 itself
rows.statement: Step 210 Section 210.20 writes E_1⇒P and E_2⇒¬P (evidence items entailing propositions); Step 210 Section 210.30, ten sections later, writes E_1=documentation (an ordinal assurance rung). Same symbol, same document, incompatible types, undisambiguated. Severity MEDIUM-HIGH.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #5 — Evidence/Test ordering reversed between Step 210's own boxed conclusion and Step 211's boxed conclusion
rows.statement: Step 210 Section 210.40 boxes Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance; Step 211 Section 211.2 boxes I->Owner->Mechanism->Test->Evidence -- directly conflicting orderings, both boxed as conclusions in consecutive files. Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple and Step 209's tail agenda both side with Step 211's ordering, so Step 210's boxed conclusion contradicts Step 210's own boxed tuple. Severity MEDIUM; the direction matters since Evidence->Test means evidence licenses the test while Test->Evidence means the test produces the evidence, which is what Steps 212-214 assume throughout.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #7 — Step 212 builds ownership diagnostics and deletes the ownership data needed to run them
rows.statement: Step 212 Section 212.15 boxes 'Ownerless Invariants' as a finding to explicitly search for (I exists but Owner(I)=empty set), yet Step 212 Section 212.4's register reprints all fifteen invariants with the Owner column removed (columns reduced to ID|Property|Target), and no search for ownerless invariants is performed anywhere in the file. Step 210's deleted Owner column contained exactly the data Sections 212.15/212.16 are designed to interrogate: 7 of 15 rows owned by a layer or pattern (effectively ownerless), 5 of 15 slash-shared. Severity HIGH.

rows.anchor: CONTRADICTION #15 — Total order on epistemic strength declined in Step 209 Section 209.21 and then used in 209.25 and 210.9
rows.statement: Step 209 Section 209.21 states Unknown≺Hypothesized≺Supported and explicitly declines a universal total ordering ('the actual epistemic lattice must be derived from the domain'). Step 209 Section 209.25 (S(T(x))>S(x)) and Step 210 Section 210.9 (Strength(T(x))>Strength(x)) both then use strict > on the same kind of quantity, presupposing the order that was just declined four sections earlier and never derived. Severity MEDIUM.

rows.statement: Inventory of new identifier families minted across Steps 208-215: I_L/I_C/I_S (3), I_KOS members (8), P_1-P_4 (4), L_1-L_2 (2), I1-I15 (15, reprinted in 212), E_1-E_5 v1 (5), A_s..A_g (6), C0-C4 (5), situations A-D (4), AuthorityLevel states (5), E_0-E_5 v2 recalibrated (6), G1-G5 (5), G-01-G-15 (15), Status(I) values (5), Gap(I) v1 (5), Gap(I) v2 different set (5), F/D/P/U (4), E_1-E_5 primary/secondary split (2), KState values (8), ELG edge types (7), 14-code type taxonomy (14), Epoch_1-Epoch_5 (5), architecture senses (4) -- totalling 162 new identifiers minted in this 8-file band, excluding one-off symbols.

rows.anchor: Collisions with prior corpus families: I1-I15 directly collides with prior I1-I20; C0-C4 collides with prior C1-C7 (and four other in-band C_n bindings)
rows.statement: The band's 162 new identifiers collide at the glyph level with at least five prior corpus invariant-naming families with zero acknowledgement: I1-I20 (prior) vs I1-I15 (Step 210/212) is a direct namespace collision with different meanings and no disambiguation; INV-1-INV-20 occupies the same conceptual space as I1-I15/I_KOS with disjoint naming; C1-C7 (prior) directly collides with C0-C4 (Step 211 criticality) and also with Step 208's contracts C_1/C_2/C_3, Step 209's contexts C, and Step 214's claims C_1/C_2 -- five bindings of C_n in the band plus the prior family; AFR-01-AFR-36 and G-01-G-15 are two parallel audit/fitness registers unaware of each other; GT/GG/GE/GC/GA collides conceptually with G1-G5, G-01-G-15, G_P, and G_i (six bindings of G total, including the Governance bounded context itself); S1-S6 collides with seven in-band bindings of S; K1-K7 collides with KState, K_t, and V_K; V1-V10 collides with V_i, the vertex set V, and the six V_C/V_K/V_I/V_E/V_T/V_F node classes. Under LATER != SUPERSEDING, none of the prior families is superseded -- the corpus now carries two or more parallel, mutually unaware invariant registries over the same architecture. Families IR/CM/LA/AAI/PLP are not mentioned, reconciled, or superseded at all.

rows.anchor: STEP 210 load-bearing boxed claims: Architectural Principle != Architectural Property (the file fails its own standard), No claim without evidence, and the assurance chain contradicted by Step 211
rows.statement: Three load-bearing boxed claims of Step 210: (1) 'Architectural Principle != Architectural Property' -- survives as the file's thesis, and the standard against which the file itself fails, since 0 of 15 invariants are shown to have an enforcement mechanism (hence 0 of 15 are properties by its own criterion). (2) 'No claim of architectural compliance without identifiable evidence' -- survives as a rule, violated in spirit by the 15-row matrix, which claims owners and verifications with zero identifiable evidence. (3) 'Invariant->Owner->Enforcement->Evidence->Test->Assurance' -- contradicted by Step 211 Section 211.2 and by Step 210's own Section 210.1 tuple (Contradiction #5).

rows.anchor: 7 individual prior-step citations across 11,287 lines — the band is a chain, not a network; the corpus baseline is unbroken
rows.statement: Machine-counted citation density across Steps 208-215: 208 cites 1 prior step (207); 209 cites 1 (208); 210 cites 1 (209); 211 cites 0; 212 cites 0 individual steps (only ranges 1-211 and 1-182); 213 cites 0 individual steps (only range 1-182); 214 cites 1 (213); 215 cites 3 (213, 73, 91) -- 7 individual citations total across 11,287 lines, one per ~1,600 lines, and 6 of the 7 are the immediately preceding step, making the band a chain rather than a network. Step 211 cites nothing, and its own 'connection to our earlier work' section names six disciplines and zero steps. Only Step 215 reaches further back than one step (to Steps 73 and 91), and both reaches carry zero content, with the Step 91 reach mismatching the real step's own title. Zero citations anywhere in the band to Steps 048, 050, 058, 082, 092, 109, 166, 025N, or Steps 205/206/207's own derived aggregates and contexts. This ~0.9-citations-per-file density is consistent with the established near-zero corpus baseline (steps 067-082 cite nothing below step 66; step 097 cites no step at all) -- the pattern is unbroken.

rows.anchor: O-9 — Step 210's matrix IS populated, but realizes only 3 of 6 declared tuple components and 0 test results.
rows.statement: 60/60 cells, 0 '?', 0 TBD -- the all-'?' pattern is broken -- but it realizes 3 of its own 6 declared tuple components, contains 15 test names and 0 test results, and only 4 of 15 invariants have a single named bounded-context owner. Seven of 15 are owned by a layer or tactical pattern (Domain, Persistence, Knowledge infrastructure, Aggregate x2, Contracts, Knowledge) -- effectively ownerless under Step 212 Section 212.15 -- and five are slash-shared, the hazard Step 212 Section 212.16 names. Row I11's owner is 'Knowledge', the exact generic object Step 208 Section 208.28 boxed a prohibition against.

rows.anchor: O-13 — Measurement discipline is bimodal: five correct refusals, six scale violations.
rows.statement: Correct refusals: Section 209.21 (declines a universal total order on epistemic states), Section 210.29 (declines to scalarize assurance, names fake precision), Section 211.4 (declines numeric gap values), Section 212.9 (six preconditions for a percentage), Section 214.23 (declines a linear KState lifecycle, permits co-occurrence), Section 215.7 (declines to convert a count into a quality score). Violations: I(A)<I(E) and L(C)=I_req-I_pres on an explicitly undefined measure (208.3/208.10, repeated 212.19, 214.7); S(T(x))>S(x) on the order 209.21 declines (209.25, 210.9); min{Assurance(...)} on the vector 211.17 forbids scalarizing (211.6); cardinal A_s=1,A_p=0 on 211.4's ordinal dimensions (211.17); Critical(I)⇒HigherAssurance(I) on the scale 210.29 declines (210.28); the proportionality on two scaleless quantities (215.10).
